units.zh: 王遜 蔡豹 羊鑒 劉胤 桓宣
units.en: Biographies grouped here open with Wang Xun, Cai Bao, Yang Jian, Liu Yin, and Huan Xuan.
units.literal: Wang Xun; Cai Bao; Yang Jian; Liu Yin; Huan Xuan.

units.zh: 〈（族子伊）〉
units.en: (Their kinsman Huan Yi)〉
units.literal: (Clansman Huan Yi)〉

units.zh: 朱伺 毛寶
units.en: Zhu Si and Mao Bao.
units.literal: Zhu Si; Mao Bao.

units.zh: 〈（子穆之）〉
units.en: (His son Mao Muzhi)〉
units.literal: (Son Mao Muzhi)〉

units.zh: 劉遐 鄧嶽
units.en: Liu Xia and Deng Yue.
units.literal: Liu Xia; Deng Yue.

units.en: (His son Deng Xia)〉
units.literal: (Son Deng Xia)〉

units.zh: 朱序
units.en: Zhu Xu.
units.literal: Zhu Xu.

units.zh: 王遜，字邵伯，魏興人也。
units.en: Wang Xun of Weixing bore the courtesy name Shaobo.
units.literal: Wang Xun, courtesy name Shaobo, was a native of Weixing.

units.zh: 仕郡察孝廉，為吏部令史，轉殿中將軍。
units.en: County nomination raised him to ministry clerk, then imperial guards captain.
units.literal: Recommended filial and incorrupt at his commandery, he served as clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and was promoted palace army commander.

units.zh: 累遷上洛太守。
units.en: He rose to governor Shangluo.
units.literal: Promoted repeatedly to administrator of Shangluo.

units.zh: 私牛馬在郡生駒犢者，秩滿悉以付官，雲是郡中所產也。
units.en: Any beasts bred under his rule he surrendered at term’s end as county-born stock.
units.literal: Private cattle and horses that foaled or calved in the commandery—when his term ended he delivered them all to the treasury, saying they were produced within the jurisdiction.

units.zh: 轉魏興太守。
units.en: Next he governed Weixing.
units.literal: Transferred to administrator of Weixing.

units.zh: 惠帝末，西南夷叛，甯州刺史李毅卒，城中百餘人奉毅女固守經年。
units.en: Southwestern tribes rose as Hui tottered; Li Yi fell at Ningzhou, leaving a hundred defenders rallying around his daughter for a year.
units.literal: Near Emperor Hui’s end southwestern barbarians rebelled; Inspector of Ningzhou Li Yi died, and little over a hundred people in the city upheld Yi’s daughter in defense for a full year.

units.zh: 永嘉四年，治中毛孟詣京師求刺史，不見省。
units.en: Yongjia 4 sent Mao Meng pleading at Luoyang—court ignored him.
units.literal: In Yongjia’s fourth year Administrator Mao Meng traveled to the capital seeking an inspector but received no audience.

units.zh: 孟固陳曰：「君亡親喪，幽閉窮城，萬里訴哀，不垂湣救。
units.en: Meng protested: “Rulers perish while cities choke—we shout leagues away yet mercy never stirs.
units.literal: Meng firmly argued: “Your lordship lost kin and lies trapped in a beleaguered city; though we wail across myriad leagues you grant no compassionate rescue.

units.zh: 既慚包胥無哭秦之感，又愧梁妻無崩城之驗，存不若亡，乞賜臣死。」
units.en: We lack Shen Baoxu’s tears before Qin or widow Liang’s collapsing grief—living now dishonors dying—strike me dead.”
units.literal: We shame Shen Baoxu who lacked tears enough for Qin and blush before Liang Qi lacking proof she collapsed walls—to survive brings less honor than death; grant me execution.”

units.zh: 朝廷憐之，乃以遜為南夷校尉、甯州刺史，使于郡便之鎮。
units.en: Moved, court named Xun southern colonel and Ningzhou inspector with mandate from county seat onward.
units.literal: The court pitied him and appointed Xun colonel of southern barbarians and inspector of Ningzhou, letting him proceed straight from the commandery to his post.

units.zh: 與孟俱行，道遇寇賊，逾年乃至。
units.en: Traveling with Meng, they met bandits on the road and took more than a year to arrive.
units.literal: Together with Meng they went; robbers waylaid them along the road—more than a year passed before arrival.

units.zh: 外逼李雄，內有夷寇，吏士散沒，城邑丘墟。
units.en: Li Xiong strangled supply lines while tribes ravaged within until garrisons vanished into ash heaps.
units.literal: Pressed by Li Xiong without and tribal raiders within, clerks and troops scattered; towns lay ruined heaps.

units.zh: 遜披荒糾厲，收聚離散，專杖威刑，鞭撻殊俗。
units.en: He hacked roads from ruin, welded law through terror, herded exiles with scourges tuned to frontier tribes.
units.literal: Xun cleared wasteland, tightened discipline, gathered refugees, relying solely on fearful punishments and flogging alien customs.

units.zh: 遜未到州，遙舉董聯為秀才，建甯功曹周悅謂聯非才，不下版檄。
units.en: Still en route he tapped Dong Lian as xiucai; Zhou Yue withheld commission.
units.literal: Before reaching the province he remotely nominated Dong Lian as cultivated talent; Jianning aide Zhou Yue judged Lian unworthy and refused to issue summons.

units.zh: 遜既到，收悅殺之。
units.en: Arrival meant Yue’s arrest and blade.
units.literal: Once arrived Xun seized Yue and executed him.

units.zh: 悅弟潛謀殺遜，以前建甯太守趙混子濤代為刺史。
units.en: Brother Qian schemed assassination and Zhao Tao’s coup.
units.literal: Yue’s brother Qian plotted to murder Xun and install Zhao Tao—son of former Jianning Administrator Zhao Hun—as inspector.

units.zh: 事覺，並誅之。
units.en: Exposure doomed every conspirator.
units.literal: The plot surfaced; all were put to death.

units.zh: 又誅豪右不奉法度者數十家。
units.en: Magnates mocking law numbered dozens beheaded.
units.literal: He further executed dozens of powerful houses that flouted statute.

units.zh: 征伐諸夷，俘馘千計，獲馬及牛羊數萬餘，於是莫不振服，威行寧土。
units.en: Frontier strikes piled trophies—thousands of skulls, myriad herds—until submission rippled province-wide.
units.literal: Campaigning against tribal bands he took heads by the thousand and horses, cattle, and sheep beyond tens of thousands—thereafter none dared resist; awe blanketed Ning lands.

units.zh: 又遣子澄奉表勸進於元帝，帝嘉之，累加散騎常侍、安南將軍、假節，校尉、刺史如故，賜爵褒中縣公。
units.en: Son Cheng’s accession memorial won stacks of titles—palace rider, southern pacifier, credential bearer—plus Baozhong duke.
units.literal: He sent son Cheng with memorial urging Yuan Di’s accession; the emperor praised him, promoting him repeatedly to palace attendant regular, general who pacifies the south, holding credential staff—colonel and inspector unchanged—with noble rank Duke of Baozhong county.

units.zh: 遜以地勢形便，上分牂柯為平夷郡，分朱提為南廣郡，分建甯為夜郎郡，分永昌為梁水郡，又改益州郡為晉寧郡，事皆施行。
units.en: He carved new commands—Pingyi, Nanguang, Yelang, Liangshui—and rechristened Yizhou as Jining—throne stamped each map.
units.literal: Judging terrain advantageous he memorialized to split Zangke into Pingyi commandery, Zhuti into Nanguang, Jianning into Yelang, Yongchang into Liangshui, and rename Yizhou commandery Jining—all approved.

units.zh: 先是，越巂太守李釗為李雄所執，自蜀逃歸，遜復以釗為越巂太守。
units.en: Li Zhao escaped Xiong’s cage to Shu margins; Xun restored his Yuegui seal.
units.literal: Earlier Administrator of Yuegui Li Zhao had been captured by Li Xiong but fled Shu back south; Xun reappointed Zhao Yuegui governor.

units.zh: 李雄遣李驤、任回攻釗，釗自南秦與漢嘉太守王載共距之，戰於溫水，釗敗績，載遂以二郡附雄。
units.en: Li Xiong sent Li Xiang and Ren Hui against Zhao; Zhao joined Hanjia administrator Wang Zai from southern Qin to resist them, fought at Warm Water, was routed, and Zai then surrendered both commanderies to Xiong.
units.literal: Li Xiong dispatched Li Xiang and Ren Hui against Zhao; Zhao joined Administrator of Hanjia Wang Zai from southern Qin to resist, fought at Warm Water, suffered rout, and Zai surrendered both commands to Xiong.

units.zh: 後驤等又渡瀘水寇寧州，遜使將軍姚崇、爨琛距之，戰於堂狼，大破驤等，崇追至瀘水，透水死者千餘人。
units.en: Xiang forded Lu and fell to Yao Chong’s Tanglang trap—corpses jammed the ford.
units.literal: Later Xiang crossed the Lu River raiding Ningzhou; Xun sent Generals Yao Chong and Cuan Chen to resist at Tanglang, crushing Xiang; Chong pursued to the Lu—over a thousand drowned crossing.

units.zh: 崇以道遠不敢渡水，遜以崇不窮追也，怒囚群帥，執崇，鞭之，怒甚，發上沖冠，冠為之裂，夜中卒。
units.en: Chong halted at Lu banks; Xun flogged him until hairpins snapped—apoplexy killed him overnight.
units.literal: Chong feared distance and dared not ford; Xun, furious he failed to pursue, imprisoned commanders, seized Chong, and flogged him—rage lifted his cap pins until the cap tore—he died that night.

units.zh: 遜在州十四年，州人復立遜中子堅行州府事。
units.en: Fourteen years later provincials raised middle heir Jian as steward.
units.literal: Xun spent fourteen years in the province; locals enthroned his middle son Jian to manage prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 詔除堅為南夷校尉、甯州刺史、假節，諡遜曰壯。
units.en: The court confirmed Jian's seal and gave Wang Xun the posthumous title Zhuang.
units.literal: An edict appointed Jian southern colonel and Ningzhou inspector with credential staff; Xun received posthumous name Zhuang.

units.zh: 陶侃懼堅不能抗對蜀人，太寧末，表以零陵太守尹奉為寧州，征堅還京，病卒。
units.en: Tao Kan doubted Jian’s spine—late Taining swapped in Yin Feng; Jian perished traveling east.
units.literal: Tao Kan feared Jian could not withstand Shu; late Taining he memorialized Lingling Administrator Yin Feng for Ningzhou and summoned Jian to the capital—Jian died en route.

units.zh: 兄澄襲爵，曆魏興太守、散騎常侍。
units.en: Brother Cheng took the dukedom through Weixing and palace posts.
units.literal: Elder brother Cheng inherited the title, serving as Weixing governor and palace attendant regular.

units.zh: 蔡豹，字士宣，陳留圉城人。
units.en: Cai Bao styled Shixuan hailed from Chenliu’s Yucheng.
units.literal: Cai Bao, courtesy name Shixuan, was from Yucheng in Chenliu.

units.zh: 高祖質，漢衛尉，左中郎將邕之叔父也。
units.en: Ancestor Zhi commanded Han guards—kin to Cai Yong.
units.literal: His ninth-generation ancestor Zhi had been Han superintendent of the guards—uncle of Palace Gentleman Cai Yong.

units.zh: 祖睦，魏尚書。
units.en: Grandfather Mu ran Wei’s secretariat.
units.literal: Grandfather Mu was Wei minister of writing.

units.zh: 父宏，陰平太守。
units.en: Father Hong held Yinping.
units.literal: Father Hong governed Yinping.

units.zh: 豹有氣幹，曆河南丞，長樂、清河太守。
units.en: Capable and bold, he filled Henan aide and twin governorships.
units.literal: Bao possessed energy and capacity; he served as aide of Henan, then administrators of Changle and Qinghe.

units.zh: 避亂南渡，元帝以為振武將軍、臨淮太守，遷建威將軍、徐州刺史。
units.en: Flight south won him rousing-might general, Linhuai governor, then building-might general atop Xuzhou.
units.literal: Fleeing turmoil southward, Yuan Di named him general who rouses might and administrator of Linhuai, later general who builds might and inspector of Xuzhou.

units.zh: 初，祖逖為徐州，豹為司馬，素易豹。
units.en: Zu Ti once commanded Xuzhou with Bao as major—Ti sneered.
units.literal: Earlier Zu Ti led Xuzhou while Bao was his adjutant—Ti had always slighted Bao.

units.zh: 至是，逖為豫州，而豹為徐州，俱受征討之寄，逖甚愧之。
units.en: Now equals in border commands, Ti smarted.
units.literal: Now Ti held Yuzhou while Bao held Xuzhou; both bore expedition mandates—Ti felt mortified.

units.zh: 是時太山太守徐龕與彭城內史劉遐同討反賊周撫於寒山，龕將於藥斬撫。
units.en: Taishan’s Xu Kan and Pengcheng’s Liu Xia attacked Zhou Fu at Hanshan; Yu Yao took Fu’s head.
units.literal: Then Taishan Administrator Xu Kan with Pengcheng interior secretary Liu Xia jointly campaigned against rebel Zhou Fu at Hanshan; Kan’s officer Yu Yao beheaded Fu.

units.zh: 及論功，而遐先之。
units.en: Credit lists placed Xia ahead.
units.literal: When merit was tallied Xia ranked first.

units.zh: 龕怒，乙太山叛，自號安北將軍、兗州刺史，攻破東莞太守侯史旄而據其塢。
units.en: Kan angrily rebelled at Taishan, styled himself General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of Yanzhou, defeated Hou Shimao, grand administrator of Dongguan, and occupied his fort.
units.literal: Kan in fury seized Taishan, rebelled, styled himself general who pacifies the north and inspector of Yanzhou, stormed Dongguan Administrator Hou Shi Mao’s fort, and seized the redoubt.

units.zh: 石季龍伐之，龕懼，求降，元帝許焉。
units.en: When Shi Hu attacked him, Kan grew frightened and sought to surrender, and Emperor Yuan accepted.
units.literal: Shi Hu attacked him; Kan feared and sued for surrender—Yuan Di accepted.

units.zh: 既而復叛歸石勒，勒遣其將王伏都、張景等數百騎助龕。
units.en: Kan flipped back to Shi Le; Le lent cavalry captains.
units.literal: Soon he rebelled again to Shi Le; Le sent generals Wang Fudu and Zhang Jing with several hundred riders to aid Kan.

units.zh: 詔征虜將軍羊鑒、武威將軍侯禮、臨淮太守劉遐、鮮卑段文鴦等與豹共討之。
units.en: Court tasked Yang Jian, Hou Li, Liu Xia, Duan Wenying, and Bao with Kan’s ruin.
units.literal: An edict ordered General Who Conquers Barbarians Yang Jian, General Who Displays Might Hou Li, Linhuai Administrator Liu Xia, Xianbei Duan Wenying and others to join Bao in punishing him.

units.zh: 諸將畏懦，頓兵下邳，不敢前。
units.en: Coalition froze at Xiapi.
units.literal: Generals cowered, halting troops at Xiapi, daring not advance.

units.zh: 豹欲進軍，鑒固不許。
units.en: Bao pressed attack; Jian vetoed.
units.literal: Bao wished to march; Jian stubbornly refused.

units.zh: 龕遣使請救於勒，勒辭以外難，而多求於龕。
units.en: Kan begged Le; Le invented excuses while squeezing tribute.
units.literal: Kan sent envoys begging rescue from Le; Le pleaded outer crises yet demanded endless gifts.

units.zh: 又王伏都等淫其室。
units.en: Le’s riders raped Kan’s women.
units.literal: Moreover Wang Fudu and cohort ravished Kan’s household.

units.zh: 龕知勒不救，且患伏都等縱暴，乃殺之，復求降。
units.en: Kan slaughtered Le’s captains and renewed capitulation.
units.literal: Kan knew Le would not save him and could not endure Fudu’s excess—he slew them and sued again to surrender.

units.zh: 元帝惡其反覆不納，敕豹、鑒以時進討。
units.en: Throne spurned another fake surrender—ordered attack.
units.literal: Yuan Di despised the flip-flopping and refused; he ordered Bao and Jian to advance on schedule.

units.zh: 鑒及劉遐等並疑憚不相聽從，互有表聞，故豹久不得進。
units.en: Mutual suspicion clogged paperwork—Bao stalled.
units.literal: Jian and Liu Xia hesitated, ignoring orders, each memorializing separately—Bao could not move for months.

units.zh: 尚書令刁協奏曰：「臣等伏思淮北征軍已失不速，今方盛暑，冒涉山險，山人便弓弩，習土俗，一人守厄，百夫不當。
units.en: Diao Xie warned: “Summer columns crossing tribal ridges face ambush archers—single chokepoints swallow armies.
units.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Diao Xie memorialized: “We reflect that the Huai-north expedition already missed speed; now midsummer forces march mountain defiles where locals wield crossbows—one man guarding a pass stops a hundred.

units.zh: 且運漕至難，一朝糧乏，非復智力所能防禦也。
units.en: River logistics snap easily—starvation erases strategy.
units.literal: Moreover river supply is desperately hard—should grain fail overnight no wit can defend.

units.zh: 《書》云寧致人，不致於人。
units.en: The 《Documents》 counsels making the foe come to you rather than rushing into his trap.
units.literal: The 《Documents》 says it is better to draw the enemy here than to be drawn there.

units.zh: 宜頓兵所在，深壁固壘，至秋不了，乃進大軍。」
units.en: Park troops, thicken walls, strike after harvest if needed.”
units.literal: We should halt where we stand, deepen walls and strengthen ramparts; if autumn ends without decision then commit the main host.”

units.zh: 詔曰：「知難而退，誠合兵家之言。
units.en: Edict answered: “Withdrawal on hardship matches canon.
units.literal: An edict replied: “Retreating when difficulty appears fits military doctrine.

units.zh: 然小賊雖狡猾，故成擒耳。
units.en: Small prey still snares.
units.literal: Yet petty bandits, however cunning, remain catchable.

units.zh: 未戰而退，先自摧衄，亦古之所忌。
units.en: Unbloodied retreat shames ancient wisdom.
units.literal: To quit without battle first breaks our own spine—also taboo in antiquity.

units.zh: 且邵存已據賊壘，威勢既振，不可退一步也。」
units.en: Shao Cun grips Kan’s nest—advance only.”
units.literal: Moreover Shao Cun already holds the rebel fort—momentum surges; not one step backward.”

units.zh: 於是遣治書御史郝嘏為行台，催攝令進討。
units.en: Therefore the court dispatched supervising secretary Hao Jia as a mobile headquarters to spur the offensive.
units.literal: Therefore they dispatched supervising secretary Hao Jia as mobile headquarters to spur the offensive.

units.zh: 豹欲徑進，鑒執不聽。
units.en: Bao demanded frontal strike—Jian blocked.
units.literal: Bao wanted a direct thrust; Jian still refused.

units.zh: 協又奏免鑒官，委豹為前鋒，以鑒兵配之，降號折沖將軍，以責後效。
units.en: Xie cashiered Jian, handed his men to Bao as crack general—demotion pending victory.
units.literal: Xie again memorialized to strip Jian’s office, appoint Bao vanguard, attach Jian’s troops to him, and demote Bao’s rank to general who smashes charge to redeem merit.

units.zh: 豹進據卞城，欲以逼龕。
units.en: Bao seized Biancheng to pinch Kan.
units.literal: Bao advanced to occupy Biancheng to press Kan.

units.zh: 時石季龍屯钜平，將攻豹，豹夜遁。
units.en: Shi Hu loomed at Juping—Bao bolted.
units.literal: Meanwhile Shi Hu camped at Juping preparing against Bao—Bao fled by night.

units.zh: 退守下邳。
units.en: He hugged Xiapi walls.
units.literal: He fell back to defend Xiapi.

units.zh: 徐龕襲取豹輜重于檀丘，將軍留寵、陸黨力戰，死之。
units.en: Kan looted Tanqiu trains—Liu Chong and Lu Dang died holding line.
units.literal: Kan raided Bao’s baggage train at Tanqiu; generals Liu Chong and Lu Dang fought to death.

units.zh: 豹既敗，將歸謝罪，北中郎王舒止之，曰：「胡寇方至，使君且當攝職，為百姓障捍。
units.en: Shu counseled: “Nomads loom—cling to command, shield folk.
units.literal: Defeated, Bao meant to return and confess; northern commander Wang Shu stopped him: “Barbarians approach—hold office awhile and shield the people.

units.zh: 賊退謝罪，不晚也。」
units.en: Resign after crisis ebbs.”
units.literal: After bandits withdraw confession will not be late.”

units.zh: 豹從之。
units.en: Bao stayed.
units.literal: Bao obeyed.

units.zh: 元帝聞豹退，使收之。
units.en: Throne ordered Bao seized.
units.literal: Yuan Di hearing of Bao’s retreat ordered his arrest.

units.zh: 使者至，王舒夜以兵圍豹，豹以為他難，率麾下擊之，聞有詔乃止。
units.en: Shu’s midnight cordon looked like mutiny until imperial voice clarified.
units.literal: Envoys arrived; Shu surrounded Bao by night—Bao mistook another crisis and struck until edict clarified.

units.zh: 舒執豹，送至建康，斬之，屍於市三日，時年五十二。
units.en: Jiankang execution followed—corpse hung market three days at fifty-two.
units.literal: Shu seized Bao, escorted him to Jiankang, executed him, exposed corpse three days—age fifty-two.

units.zh: 豹在徐土，內撫將士，外懷諸眾，甚得遠近情，聞其死，多悼惜之。
units.en: Soldiers and settlers mourned his fairness.
units.literal: In Xu lands Bao soothed troops within and tribes without—north and south cherished him; mourning spread at news of death.

units.zh: 無子，兄子裔字元子，散騎常侍、兗州刺史、高陽鄉侯。
units.en: Nephew Yi inherited fame—palace rider, Yanzhou inspector, Gaoyang marquis.
units.literal: Childless, nephew Yi styled Yuanzi became palace attendant regular, inspector of Yanzhou, Marquis of Gaoyang township.

units.zh: 殷浩北伐，使裔率眾出彭城，卒於軍。
units.en: Yin Hao’s war consumed Yi at Pengcheng.
units.literal: Yin Hao’s northern expedition sent Yi leading troops from Pengcheng—he died in camp.

units.zh: 羊鑒，字景期，太山人也。
units.en: Yang Jian, styled Jingqi, came from Taishan commandery.
units.literal: Yang Jian, courtesy name Jingqi, was a native of Taishan.

units.zh: 父濟，匈奴中郎將。
units.en: His father Ji had been Central Commandant of the Xiongnu.
units.literal: His father Ji was Central Commandant of the Xiongnu.

units.zh: 兄煒，曆太僕、兗徐二州刺史。
units.en: His elder brother Wei had held the imperial stud ministry and the inspectorates of Yan and Xu.
units.literal: His elder brother Wei successively served as Minister of the Imperial Stud and Inspector of Yan and Xu provinces.

units.zh: 鑒為東陽太守，累遷太子左衛率。
units.en: Yang Jian governed Dongyang and rose to left commander of the crown prince's guard.
units.literal: Jian served as Administrator of Dongyang and was promoted to Left Commander of the Crown Prince's Guard.

units.zh: 時徐龕反叛，司徒王導以鑒是龕州裏冠族，必能制之，請遣北討。
units.en: When Xu Kan rebelled, Wang Dao argued that Yang Jian, foremost clan of Kan's home province, could master him and asked that he be sent north.
units.literal: When Xu Kan rebelled, Minister of Education Wang Dao held that Jian, as the leading clan of Kan's province, would surely be able to control him, and requested that he be sent north to campaign.

units.zh: 鑒深辭才非將帥。
units.en: Yang Jian refused firmly, protesting that he was no general.
units.literal: Jian firmly declined, saying he lacked the talent of a commander.

units.zh: 太尉郗鑒亦表謂鑒非才，不宜妄使。
units.en: Grand Commandant Xi Jian likewise warned that Yang Jian was unfit for the post.
units.literal: Grand Commandant Xi Jian also memorialized that Jian lacked ability and should not be rashly employed.

units.zh: 導不納，強啟授以征討都督，果敗績。
units.en: Wang Dao overruled them, pushed the appointment as superintendent of punitive campaigns, and defeat followed.
units.literal: Dao would not accept this; he forcefully memorialized and had him appointed Superintendent of Punitive Campaigns, with defeat the result.

units.zh: 導以舉鑒非才，請自貶，帝不從。
units.en: Wang Dao asked to demote himself for misjudging Yang Jian; the emperor refused.
units.literal: Dao, for having recommended Jian though he lacked talent, asked to demote himself; the Emperor did not agree.

units.zh: 有司正鑒斬刑，元帝詔以鑒太妃外屬，特免死，除名。
units.en: Officials sought Yang Jian's head, but Emperor Yuan spared him as a maternal kinsman of the grand consort and struck his name from office.
units.literal: The authorities judged Jian deserving of execution by decapitation; Emperor Yuan issued an edict that because Jian was a maternal relative of the Grand Consort, he was specially spared death and struck from the rolls.

units.zh: 久之，為少府。
units.en: Years later he was named minister of the palace economy.
units.literal: After a long while he became Minister of the Palace Economy.

units.zh: 及王敦反，明帝以鑒敦舅，又素相親黨，微被嫌責。
units.en: When Wang Dun rebelled, Emperor Ming eyed Yang Jian as Dun's uncle and old ally and lightly censured him.
units.literal: When Wang Dun rebelled, Emperor Ming, because Jian was Dun's maternal uncle and had long been intimate with his faction, was slightly suspected and reproached.

units.zh: 及成帝即位，豫討蘇峻，以功封豐城縣侯，徙光祿勳，卒。
units.en: Under Emperor Cheng he helped crush Su Jun, won Fengcheng marquisate, became superintendent of the imperial household, and died.
units.literal: When Emperor Cheng ascended the throne, Jian took part in punishing Su Jun; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Fengcheng county, transferred to Superintendent of the Imperial Household, and died.

units.zh: 劉胤，字承胤，東萊掖人，漢齊悼惠王肥之後也，美姿容，善自任遇，交結時豪，名著海岱間，士咸慕之。
units.en: Liu Yin, courtesy Chengyin, of Ye in Donglai—descendant of Han Prince Dao-Hui of Qi—was handsome and self-assured, befriended the magnates of his day, and won fame between the sea and Mount Tai so that scholars all admired him.
units.literal: Liu Yin, courtesy name Chengyin, was from Ye in Donglai—descended from Han Prince Dao-Hui of Qi—handsome, confident, befriended magnates, famed between sea and Tai heights—scholars idolized him.

units.zh: 舉賢良，辟司空掾，並不就。
units.en: Court nominations went unanswered.
units.literal: Recommended worthy and incorrupt, summoned aide to the minister of works—he accepted neither.

units.zh: 且天下大亂，攜母欲避地遼東，路經幽州，刺史王浚留胤，表為渤海太守。
units.en: Flight toward Liaodong trapped him under Wang Jun’s Bohai appointment.
units.literal: As chaos engulfed the realm he escorted mother toward Liaodong; passing Youzhou Inspector Wang Jun detained Yin, memorializing him administrator of Bohai.

units.zh: 浚敗，轉依冀州刺史邵續。
units.en: Jun’s collapse drove him to Shao Xu.
units.literal: After Jun fell he attached to Ji Inspector Shao Xu.

units.zh: 續徒眾寡弱，謀降于石勒，胤言于續曰：「夫田單、包胥，齊楚之小吏耳，猶能存已滅之邦，全喪敗之國。
units.en: Yin pleaded: “Tian Dan and Shen Baoxu were clerks yet rebuilt kingdoms.
units.literal: Xu’s host was weak and plotted surrender to Shi Le; Yin told Xu: “Tian Dan and Shen Baoxu were petty clerks of Qi and Chu yet restored extinguished states and rescued ruined realms.

units.zh: 今將軍杖精銳之眾，居全勝之城，如何墜將登之功於一蕢，委忠信之人於豺狼乎！
units.en: Why junk victory-in-hand to jackals?
units.literal: Now you wield crack troops inside an undefeated city—how cast aside merit nearing crown for one basketful or abandon loyal hearts to jackals!

units.zh: 且項羽、袁紹非不強也，高祖縞冠，人應如響；
units.en: Moreover Xiang Yu and Yuan Shao were hardly weak—yet Gaozu in a hemp cap drew followers like echoes;
units.literal: Moreover Xiang Yu and Yuan Shao were hardly weak—yet Gaozu in hemp cap drew responses like echoes;

units.zh: 曹公奉帝，而諸侯綏穆。
units.en: Cao Cao’s imperial puppet soothed lords.
units.literal: Cao Cao upheld the emperor and lords grew calm.

units.zh: 何者？
units.en: Why?
units.literal: Why?

units.zh: 蓋逆順之理殊，自然之數定也。
units.en: Righteous mandate decides fate.
units.literal: Because principle of rebellion versus loyalty differs—Heaven’s arithmetic fixes outcome.

units.zh: 況夷戎丑類，屯結無賴，雖有犬羊之盛，終有庖宰之患，而欲托根結援，無乃殆哉！」
units.en: Alien packs swarm yet await slaughter—allying courts doom.”
units.literal: How much more barbarian scum huddling without honor—though numerous as dogs and sheep they face butcher’s block—yet you would root with them—perilous indeed!”

units.zh: 續曰：「若如君言，計將安出？」
units.en: Xu pressed strategy.”
units.literal: Xu asked, “If so, what plan?”

units.zh: 胤曰：「琅邪王以聖德欽明，創基江左，中興之隆可企踵而待。
units.en: Yin said, "The Prince of Langya shines with sagely virtue, founding the realm east of the Yangzi—the glory of restoration is within reach.
units.literal: Yin answered: “Prince Langya shines with sagely virtue, founding east of the Yangzi—restoration stands within sight.

units.zh: 今為將軍計者，莫若抗大順以激義士之心，奉忠正以厲軍人之志。
units.en: For the general now, nothing surpasses upholding grand legitimacy to stir gentlemen's hearts and displaying loyalty to steel soldiers' resolve.
units.literal: For the general now nothing surpasses upholding grand legitimacy to stir gentlemen’s hearts and displaying loyalty to steel soldiers’ resolve.

units.zh: 夫機事在密，時至難違，存亡廢興，在此舉矣。」
units.en: Opportunity lies in secrecy; the moment is hard to refuse—survival or ruin hangs on this act."
units.literal: Opportunity lies in secrecy; moments flee—survival or ruin hangs on this act.”

units.zh: 續從之，乃殺異議者數人，遣使江南，朝廷嘉之。
units.en: Xu slew doubters, hailed Jin court—praise followed.
units.literal: Xu followed—executed dissenters, sent envoys south—the court praised him.

units.zh: 胤仍求自行，續厚遣之。
units.en: Liu Yin again asked to travel on his own behalf, and Shao Xu sent him off with generous support.
units.literal: Yin still asked to go in person, and Xu generously sent him forth.

units.zh: 既至，元帝命為丞相參軍，累遷尚書吏部郎。
units.en: Once he reached the court, Emperor Yuan appointed him aide to the Chancellor of State and later promoted him repeatedly to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
units.literal: When he had arrived, Emperor Yuan ordered him to be an aide to the Chancellor of State; he was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 胤聞石季龍攻厭次，言於元帝曰：「北方鎮皆沒，惟余邵續而已。
units.en: When Liu Yin learned that Shi Jilong was assaulting Yanqi, he told Emperor Yuan: "Every northern bastion is gone except Shao Xu.
units.literal: Yin heard that Shi Jilong was attacking Yanqi and said to Emperor Yuan: "The northern garrison towns have all fallen; only Shao Xu remains.

units.zh: 如使君為季龍所制，孤義士之心，阻歸本之路。
units.en: If you fall under Jilong's thumb, you will strand loyal hearts and cut off the routes home for those who would serve the dynasty.
units.literal: If you, sir, were restrained by Jilong, you would isolate the hearts of righteous men and block the roads by which they return to allegiance.

units.zh: 愚謂宜存救援。」
units.en: In my humble view we should send relief and keep him alive."
units.literal: In my foolish opinion it is fitting to preserve him with rescue."

units.zh: 元帝將遣救之，會續已沒而止。
units.en: Emperor Yuan was ready to send aid, but Shao Xu had already fallen, so the plan was dropped.
units.literal: Emperor Yuan was about to dispatch rescue when it happened that Xu had already perished, so he desisted.

units.zh: 王敦素與胤交，甚欽貴之，請為右司馬。
units.en: Wang Dun had always been close to Liu Yin and held him in high regard; he asked to have Yin serve as Right Major Clerk.
units.literal: Wang Dun had long been on friendly terms with Yin and greatly esteemed him; he requested Yin as Right Major Clerk.

units.zh: 胤知敦有不臣心，枕疾不視事，以是忤敦意，出為豫章太守，辭以腳疾，詔就家授印綬。
units.en: Liu Yin saw that Wang Dun nursed treasonous ambitions, so he stayed bedridden and refused to handle affairs; Wang Dun took offense, transferred him to Yuzhang as administrator, and when Yin cited bad feet the throne ordered the seals delivered to his house regardless.
units.literal: Yin knew Dun harbored a heart not loyal to the throne, so he feigned illness on his pillow and avoided duty; thereby offending Dun's wishes, he was sent out as Administrator of Yuzhang; pleading foot ailment, he declined, but an edict ordered the seal cord conferred at his home.

units.zh: 郡人莫鴻，南土豪族，因亂，殺本縣令，橫恣無道，百姓患之。
units.en: Mo Hong of the commandery, a wealthy southern magnate, used the chaos to murder the sitting magistrate and terrorized the district until the people groaned under him.
units.literal: A man of the commandery named Mo Hong, a powerful southern clan, exploited the turmoil to kill the county magistrate; he behaved lawlessly and the common people suffered.

units.zh: 胤至，誅鴻及諸豪右，界內肅然。
units.en: Liu Yin executed Mo Hong and the rest of the local strongmen, and the jurisdiction fell quiet.
units.literal: When Yin arrived, he executed Hong and the leading magnates, and within his borders all was orderly.

units.zh: 咸和初，為平南軍司，加散騎常侍。
units.en: Early in the Xianhe reign he was named army supervisor under the general Who Pacifies the South and was also given the title of ordinary attendant cavalier at court.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Xianhe era he became Army Supervisor of the South Pacifying Army with additional appointment as Palace Attendant Cavalier in Ordinary Attendance.

units.zh: 蘇峻作亂，溫嶠率眾而下，留胤等守溢口。
units.en: During Su Jun's revolt, Wen Qiao marched downstream while Liu Yin and others were left to hold Yikou.
units.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Wen Qiao led the host downstream and left Yin and others to guard Yikou.

units.zh: 事平，以勳賜爵豐城子。
units.en: After peace returned he received the merit title of Viscount of Fengcheng.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, he was granted the noble rank Viscount of Fengcheng for merit.

units.zh: 俄而代嶠為平南將軍、都督江州諸軍事、領江州刺史、假節。
units.en: Before long he replaced Wen Qiao as general Who Pacifies the South, governor of Jiangzhou military affairs, inspector of the province, and bearer of the credential staff.
units.literal: Soon he succeeded Qiao as general Who Pacifies the South, commander of all military affairs of Jiangzhou, concurrent Inspector of Jiangzhou, and credential staff.

units.zh: 胤位任轉高，矜豪日甚，縱酒耽樂，不恤政事，大殖財貨，商販百萬。
units.en: Power went to Liu Yin's head: he drank and reveled, ignored administration, hoarded coin, and ran merchant ventures worth millions.
units.literal: As Yin's rank and duties rose higher, his arrogance grew daily; he gave himself to wine and pleasure, neglected government, amassed vast wealth, and traded goods worth millions.

units.zh: 初，胤之代嶠也，遠近皆為謂非選。
units.en: When Liu Yin first stepped into Wen Qiao's shoes, everyone near and far agreed it was the wrong choice.
units.literal: At first, when Yin succeeded Qiao, those near and far all said it was not the right appointment.

units.zh: 陶侃、郗鑒咸雲胤非方伯才，朝廷不從。
units.en: Tao Kan and Xi Jian both warned that Liu Yin was no provincial governor, yet the court brushed them aside.
units.literal: Tao Kan and Xi Jian both said Yin lacked the talent of a regional governor; the court did not comply.

units.zh: 或問王悅曰：「今大難之後，綱紀弛頓，自江陵至於建康三千餘里，流人萬計，布在江州。
units.en: A courtier asked Wang Yue: "The realm has barely survived disaster; from Jiangling to Jiankang—over three thousand li—discipline is frayed and tens of thousands of refugees blanket Jiangzhou.
units.literal: Someone asked Wang Yue: "After this great calamity, laws and discipline are slack; from Jiangling to Jiankang, more than three thousand li, displaced people number in the tens of thousands and are spread across Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 江州，國之南籓，要害之地，而胤以侈忲之性，臥而對之，不有外變，必有內患。」
units.en: Jiangzhou is the dynasty's southern shield, yet Liu Yin, vain and domineering, lounges over it; even without foreign attack, trouble will brew within."
units.literal: Jiangzhou is the southern bulwark of the state, a place of vital importance; yet Yin, by nature extravagant and overbearing, lies idle over it—if no external crisis arises, there will surely be internal trouble."

units.zh: 悅曰：「聞溫平南語家公雲，連得惡夢，思見代者。
units.en: Wang Yue replied: "Minister Wen told my father he suffered nightmares and wanted a successor.
units.literal: Yue said: "I heard Minister Who Pacifies the South Wen tell my father that he kept having nightmares and wished to see someone replace him.

units.zh: 尋雲可用劉胤。
units.en: Soon afterward he named Liu Yin as acceptable.
units.literal: Shortly afterward he said Liu Yin could be used.

units.zh: 此乃溫意，非家公也。」
units.en: That was Wen Qiao's notion, not my father's judgment."
units.literal: That was Wen's idea, not my father's."

units.zh: 是時朝廷空罄，百官無祿，惟資江州運漕。
units.en: The treasury was bare and no salary reached the ministers; everyone lived off grain convoys from Jiangzhou.
units.literal: At that time the court treasury was empty and officials received no salaries; it depended solely on grain shipments from Jiangzhou.

units.zh: 而胤商旅繼路，以私廢公。
units.en: Meanwhile Liu Yin's trading trains clogged the highways and private gain trumped the public good.
units.literal: Yet Yin's merchant convoys crowded the roads, putting private profit ahead of public duty.

units.zh: 有司奏免胤官。
units.en: The bureaus memorialized to strip Liu Yin of his post.
units.literal: The relevant offices memorialized to dismiss Yin from office.

units.zh: 書始下，而胤為郭默所害，年四十九。
units.en: The edict had scarcely gone out when Guo Mo killed him; Liu Yin was forty-nine.
units.literal: The document had barely been issued when Yin was murdered by Guo Mo; he was forty-nine.

units.zh: 子赤松嗣，尚南平長公主，位至黃門郎、義興太守。
units.en: His heir Chisong succeeded to the title, married the Princess of Nanping, and reached the offices of palace gentleman and administrator of Yixing.
units.literal: His son Chisong inherited the title, married the Eldest Princess of Nanping, and rose to Palace Gentleman and Administrator of Yixing.

units.zh: 桓宣，譙國銍人也。
units.en: Huan Xuan came from Zhi in Qiao commandery.
units.literal: Huan Xuan was a man of Zhi in the Principality of Qiao.

units.zh: 祖詡，義陽太守。
units.en: His grandfather Huan Xu had served as administrator of Yiyang.
units.literal: His grandfather Xu was Administrator of Yiyang.

units.zh: 父弼，冠軍長史。
units.en: His father Huan Bi was chief clerk on the staff of the Champion general.
units.literal: His father Bi was Chief Clerk to the Champion general.

units.zh: 宣開濟篤素，為元帝丞相舍人。
units.en: Huan Xuan was generous, steady, and unpretentious, and he became a secretary under Emperor Yuan's chancellor.
units.literal: Xuan was openhanded, earnest, and plain; he served as a secretary to Emperor Yuan's Chancellor of State.

units.zh: 時塢主張平自稱豫州刺史，樊雅自號譙郡太守，各據一城，眾數千人。
units.en: The stockade chief Zhang Ping claimed the title of inspector of Yuzhou while Fan Ya styled himself administrator of Qiao; each held a citadel and commanded several thousand men.
units.literal: At that time the fort master Zhang Ping styled himself Inspector of Yuzhou and Fan Ya called himself Administrator of the Principality of Qiao; each held one walled town with several thousand followers.

units.zh: 帝以宣信厚，又與平、雅同州裏，轉宣為參軍，使就平、雅。
units.en: Emperor Yuan trusted Huan Xuan's integrity and their common roots with Zhang Ping and Fan Ya, so he moved Xuan onto staff duty and sent him to treat with the pair.
units.literal: The emperor, trusting Xuan's honesty and knowing he shared a homeland with Ping and Ya, transferred Xuan to be an aide and sent him to Ping and Ya.

units.zh: 平、雅遣軍主簿隨宣詣丞相府受節度，帝皆加四品將軍，即其所部，使捍禦北方。
units.en: Zhang Ping and Fan Ya sent regimental clerks to escort Huan Xuan to the chancellor's office for orders; the emperor named each a fourth-rank general over his own men to hold the northern frontier.
units.literal: Ping and Ya dispatched their army clerks to accompany Xuan to the Chancellor's residence to receive orders; the emperor promoted each to general of the fourth rank over their own troops to shield the north.

units.zh: 南中郎將王含請宣為參軍。
units.en: Wang Han, general Who Guards the South, asked for Huan Xuan as an aide.
units.literal: General Who Guards the South Wang Han requested Xuan as an aide.

units.zh: 頃之，豫州刺史祖逖出屯蘆洲，遣參軍殷乂詣平、雅。
units.en: Soon Zu Ti, inspector of Yuzhou, advanced to Luzhou and sent his aide Yin Yi to Zhang Ping and Fan Ya.
units.literal: Before long, Inspector of Yuzhou Zu Ti advanced and camped at Luzhou, sending aide Yin Yi to Ping and Ya.

units.zh: 乂意輕平，視其屋，雲當持作馬廄，見大鑊，欲鑄作鐵器。
units.en: Yin Yi treated Zhang Ping with contempt, sized up his halls as future horse stalls, and eyed a ritual cauldron as scrap iron.
units.literal: Yi looked down on Ping; surveying his houses, he said they ought to be turned into stables, and seeing a great cauldron he wished to melt it for iron tools.

units.zh: 平曰：「此是帝王大鑊，天下定後方當用之，奈何打破！」
units.en: Zhang Ping cried: "That is the imperial cauldron for the day the realm is pacified—how dare you break it!"
units.literal: Ping said: "This is the emperor's great cauldron; only after the realm is settled should it be used—how can you smash it!"

units.zh: 乂曰：「卿能保頭不？
units.en: Yin Yi shot back: "Can you even keep your head?
units.literal: Yi said: "Can you even keep your head?

units.zh: 而惜大鑊邪！」
units.en: And you worry about a kettle!"
units.literal: And you fret over a great cauldron!"

units.zh: 平大怒，於坐斬乂，阻兵固守。
units.en: Zhang Ping flew into a rage, executed Yin Yi at the table, and shut his gates for war.
units.literal: Ping was furious and beheaded Yi at the banquet; then he barred his gates with arms.

units.zh: 歲餘，逖攻平殺之，而雅據譙城。
units.en: A year later Zu Ti assaulted Zhang Ping and slew him while Fan Ya still held Qiao.
units.literal: After more than a year Ti attacked Ping and killed him, while Ya held Qiao city.

units.zh: 逖以力弱，求助於含，含遣宣領兵五百助逖。
units.en: Zu Ti's forces were thin, so he begged Wang Han for help; Han detached Huan Xuan with five hundred soldiers.
units.literal: Ti, being weak in strength, sought help from Han; Han sent Xuan with five hundred men to aid Ti.

units.zh: 逖謂宣曰：「卿先已說平、雅，信義大著於彼。
units.en: Zu Ti told Huan Xuan: "You already won Zhang Ping and Fan Ya with your word; your honor shines there.
units.literal: Ti said to Xuan: "You have already persuaded Ping and Ya; your good faith is famed among them.

units.zh: 今復為我說雅。
units.en: Go speak to Fan Ya again on my behalf.
units.literal: Now speak again to Ya for me.

units.zh: 雅若降者，方相擢用，不但免死而已。」
units.en: If Fan Ya yields, he will be lifted up and employed, not merely spared execution."
units.literal: If Ya submits, he will be promoted and employed—not merely spared death."

units.zh: 宣復單馬從兩人詣雅，曰：「祖逖方欲平蕩二寇，每何卿為援。
units.en: Huan Xuan rode again with only two followers and said: "Zu Ti means to crush both rebels and leans on you again and again as his ally.
units.literal: Xuan again rode alone with two men to Ya and said: "Zu Ti intends to wipe out the two bandits and repeatedly looks to you as reinforcement.

units.zh: 前殷乂輕薄，非豫州意。
units.en: Yin Yi's insults were his alone; they were not Zu Ti's wish.
units.literal: Earlier Yin Yi was rude and shallow; that was not the Inspector's intent.

units.zh: 今若和解，則忠勳可立，富貴可保。
units.en: Make peace now and you can win lasting merit and keep rank and riches.
units.literal: If you reconcile now, loyal merit can be established and honor and wealth preserved.

units.zh: 若猶固執，東府赫然更遣猛將，以卿烏合之眾，憑阻窮城，強賊伺其北，國家攻其南，萬無一全也。
units.en: If you cling to defiance, the eastern command will answer with seasoned generals; trapped in a broken wall with raiders to your north and imperial troops to your south, almost none of you would survive.
units.literal: If you still stubbornly resist, the eastern headquarters will surely send fierce generals in wrath—with your mob crowding a ruined town, strong bandits watching from the north and the state striking from the south, not one in ten thousand would survive.

units.zh: 願善量之。」
units.en: Think it through carefully."
units.literal: I urge you to weigh this carefully."

units.zh: 雅與宣置酒結友，遣子隨宣詣逖。
units.en: Fan Ya drank with Huan Xuan, pledged friendship, and sent his son back with him to Zu Ti.
units.literal: Ya feasted with Xuan and sealed friendship, then sent his son with Xuan to Zu Ti.

units.zh: 少日，雅便自詣逖，逖遣雅還撫其眾。
units.en: Days later Fan Ya presented himself to Zu Ti, who sent him home to steady his troops.
units.literal: Within days Ya went himself to Ti; Ti sent Ya back to reassure his followers.

units.zh: 雅僉謂前數罵辱，懼罪不敢降。
units.en: Fan Ya remembered how often he had abused them and feared reprisal, so he hesitated to yield.
units.literal: Ya altogether considered how he had repeatedly reviled them earlier and feared punishment, so he dared not surrender.

units.zh: 雅復閉城自守。
units.en: Fan Ya slammed the gates shut once more.
units.literal: Ya closed the city again and held out.

units.zh: 逖往攻之，復遣宣入說雅。
units.en: Zu Ti besieged him and again slipped Huan Xuan inside to argue the point.
units.literal: Ti attacked him and again sent Xuan inside to persuade Ya.

units.zh: 雅即斬異己者，遂出降。
units.en: Fan Ya killed the doubters among his officers and marched out to capitulate.
units.literal: Ya immediately executed dissenters and then came out to surrender.

units.zh: 未幾，石勒別將圍譙城，含又遣宣率眾救逖，未至而賊退。
units.en: Soon one of Shi Le's lieutenants surrounded Qiao; Wang Han again ordered Huan Xuan forward, though the raiders melted away before he arrived.
units.literal: Before long, Shi Le's detached commander besieged Qiao city; Han again sent Xuan with troops to rescue Ti, but the bandits withdrew before they arrived.

units.zh: 逖留宣討諸未服，皆破之。
units.en: Zu Ti retained Huan Xuan to mop up holdouts, and he shattered every pocket of resistance.
units.literal: Ti kept Xuan to subdue those still unsubmissive; Xuan broke them all.

units.zh: 遷譙國內史。
units.en: He rose to interior secretary of Qiao.
units.literal: He was promoted to Interior Secretary of the Principality of Qiao.

units.zh: 祖約之棄譙城也，宣以箋諫，不從，由是石勒遂有陳留。
units.en: When Zu Yue quit Qiao, Huan Xuan wrote to dissuade him; Yue refused, and Shi Le seized Chenliu.
units.literal: When Zu Yue abandoned Qiao city, Xuan remonstrated by letter; Yue did not listen, whereupon Shi Le gained Chenliu.

units.zh: 及約與蘇峻同反，宣謂祖智曰：「今強胡未滅，將戮力以討之，而與峻俱反，此安得久乎！
units.en: After Zu Yue sided with Su Jun, Huan Xuan warned Zu Zhi: "The northern tribes still threaten us—we should unite against them, yet you rise with Su Jun; how long can that endure?
units.literal: When Yue joined Su Jun in rebellion, Xuan said to Zu Zhi: "The fierce Hu are not yet destroyed; we ought to combine strength to strike them—yet you rebel alongside Jun; how can that last!

units.zh: 使君若欲為雄霸，何不助國討峻，威名自舉。」
units.en: If you crave dominance, why not help the court crush Su Jun and earn fame in the bargain?"
units.literal: If you, sir, wish to play the warlord, why not aid the state in attacking Jun and raise your own renown?"

units.zh: 智等不能用。
units.en: Zu Zhi and his circle ignored him.
units.literal: Zhi and the others would not heed him.

units.zh: 宣欲諫約，遣其子戎白約求入。
units.en: Huan Xuan meant to confront Zu Yue directly and sent his son Huan Rong to ask leave to enter camp.
units.literal: Xuan wished to remonstrate with Yue and sent his son Rong to tell Yue he sought entry.

units.zh: 約知宣必諫，不聽。
units.en: Zu Yue knew Huan Xuan would lecture him and barred the gate.
units.literal: Yue knew Xuan would surely remonstrate and refused to hear him.

units.zh: 宣遂距約，不與之同。
units.en: Huan Xuan therefore opposed Zu Yue and refused the rebellion.
units.literal: Xuan therefore resisted Yue and would not join him.

units.zh: 邵陵人陳光率部落數百家降宣，宣皆慰撫之。
units.en: Chen Guang of Shaoling brought hundreds of clan families over to Huan Xuan, who welcomed and settled them.
units.literal: Chen Guang of Shaoling led several hundred clan households to surrender to Xuan; Xuan comforted them all.

units.zh: 約還曆陽，宣將數千家欲南投尋陽，營於馬頭山。
units.en: Zu Yue withdrew to Liyang while Huan Xuan guided several thousand households toward Xunyang and pitched camp at Mount Matou.
units.literal: Yue returned to Liyang; Xuan led several thousand families intending to flee south to Xunyang and camped at Mount Matou.

units.zh: 值祖煥欲襲湓口，陶侃使毛寶救之。
units.en: Zu Huan chose that moment to strike Yikou, so Tao Kan dispatched Mao Bao to relieve it.
units.literal: It happened that Zu Huan meant to raid Yikou; Tao Kan sent Mao Bao to rescue it.

units.zh: 煥遣眾攻宣，宣使戎求救於寶。
units.en: Zu Huan assaulted Huan Xuan, who sent Huan Rong to beg Mao Bao for rescue.
units.literal: Zu Huan sent troops to attack Xuan; Xuan had Rong seek aid from Bao.

units.zh: 寶擊煥，破之，宣因投溫嶠。
units.en: Mao Bao smashed Zu Huan's force, after which Huan Xuan threw in with Wen Qiao.
units.literal: Bao struck Zu Huan and defeated him; Xuan therefore joined Wen Qiao.

units.zh: 嶠以戎為參軍。
units.en: Wen Qiao named Huan Rong his aide.
units.literal: Qiao appointed Rong as an aide.

units.zh: 賊平，宣居於武昌，戎復為劉胤參軍。
units.en: When the rebellion ended Huan Xuan stayed at Wuchang; Huan Rong later served Liu Yin as aide.
units.literal: After the rebels were crushed, Xuan dwelt at Wuchang; Rong again became Liu Yin's aide.

units.zh: 郭默害胤，復以戎為參軍。
units.en: After Guo Mo assassinated Liu Yin he pressed Huan Rong back into service.
units.literal: When Guo Mo murdered Yin, he again took Rong as aide.

units.zh: 陶侃討默，默遣戎求救于宣，宣偽許之。
units.en: Tao Kan's expedition against Guo Mo prompted Mo to send Huan Rong to plead with Huan Xuan, who promised aid he never meant to give.
units.literal: When Tao Kan attacked Mo, Mo sent Rong to beg rescue from Xuan; Xuan falsely promised help.

units.zh: 西陽太守鄧岳、武昌太守劉詡皆疑宣與默同。
units.en: Deng Yue of Xiyang and Liu Xu of Wuchang suspected Huan Xuan of colluding with Guo Mo.
units.literal: Administrator of Xiyang Deng Yue and Administrator of Wuchang Liu Xu both suspected Xuan of siding with Mo.

units.zh: 豫州西曹王隨曰：「宣尚背祖約，何緣同郭默邪！」
units.en: Wang Sui, a western bureau clerk at Yuzhou, argued: "Huan Xuan already broke with Zu Yue—why would he now back Guo Mo?"
units.literal: Western Bureau clerk Wang Sui of Yuzhou said: "Xuan once turned against Zu Yue—why would he align with Guo Mo!"

units.zh: 嶽、詡乃遣隨詣宣以觀之。
units.en: Deng Yue and Liu Xu therefore dispatched Wang Sui to watch Huan Xuan.
units.literal: Yue and Xu therefore sent Sui to Xuan to observe him.

units.zh: 隨謂宣曰：「明府心雖不爾，無以自明，惟有以戎付隨耳。」
units.en: Wang Sui told him: "Even if your heart is clean, you cannot prove it—give me Huan Rong if you want trust."
units.literal: Sui said to Xuan: "Though your heart is not so, you cannot prove it yourself—your only course is to hand Rong over to me."

units.zh: 宣乃遣戎與隨俱迎陶侃。
units.en: Huan Xuan released Huan Rong to accompany Wang Sui to Tao Kan.
units.literal: Xuan then sent Rong with Sui together to welcome Tao Kan.

units.zh: 辟戎為掾，上宣為武昌太守。
units.en: Tao Kan enrolled Huan Rong as aide and memorialized Huan Xuan as administrator of Wuchang.
units.literal: Kan recruited Rong as an aide and memorialized Xuan as Administrator of Wuchang.

units.zh: 尋遷監沔中軍事、南中郎將、江夏相。
units.en: Soon he supervised Han River defenses as general of the southern central court and chancellor of Jiangxia while keeping his former rank.
units.literal: Soon he was promoted to supervise military affairs on the Han River, General Who Guards the Center of the South, Chancellor of Jiangxia, as before.

units.zh: 石勒荊州刺史郭敬戍襄陽。
units.en: Guo Jing, whom Shi Le had named inspector of Jingzhou, held Xiangyang.
units.literal: Shi Le's Inspector of Jingzhou, Guo Jing, garrisoned Xiangyang.

units.zh: 陶侃使其子平西參軍斌與宣俱攻樊城，拔之。
units.en: Tao Kan sent his son Tao Bin, aide to the general Who Pacifies the West, to join Huan Xuan against Fancheng; they captured it.
units.literal: Tao Kan sent his son Bin, aide to the general Who Pacifies the West, to attack Fancheng jointly with Xuan and took it.

units.zh: 竟陵太守李陽又破新野。
units.en: Li Yang, administrator of Jingling, routed the enemy again at Xinye.
units.literal: Administrator of Jingling Li Yang again defeated them at Xinye.

units.zh: 敬懼，遁走。
units.en: Guo Jing panicked and ran.
units.literal: Jing feared this and fled.

units.zh: 宣與陽遂平襄陽，侃使宣鎮之，以其淮南部曲立義成郡。
units.en: Huan Xuan and Li Yang secured Xiangyang; Tao Kan told Huan Xuan to stay as commander and carved Yicheng commandery from his Huai River veterans.
units.literal: Xuan and Yang thereupon pacified Xiangyang; Kan ordered Xuan to hold it and established Yicheng Commandery from his Huai-nan personal corps.

units.zh: 宣招懷初附，勸課農桑，簡刑罰，略威儀，或載鋤耒於軺軒，或親芸獲於隴畝。
units.en: He soothed new subjects, pushed farming and silk culture, eased penalties, dropped pomp—sometimes hauling hoes in his coach, sometimes reaping beside peasants.
units.literal: Xuan summoned and soothed the newly attached, urged farming and sericulture, simplified punishments, relaxed ceremony—sometimes carrying hoes and plows in his light carriage, sometimes harvesting with his own hands in the fields.

units.zh: 十餘年間，石季龍再遣騎攻之，宣能得眾心，每以寡弱距守，論者以為次於祖逖、周訪。
units.en: Across ten years Shi Jilong hurled two cavalry campaigns at him; Huan Xuan kept popular devotion and turned back superior numbers—commentators placed him just below Zu Ti and Zhou Fang.
units.literal: Within a dozen years Shi Jilong twice sent cavalry against him; Xuan won the people's hearts and each time repelled far stronger foes with scant forces—critics ranked him second only to Zu Ti and Zhou Fang.

units.zh: 侃方欲使宣北事中原，會侃薨。
units.en: Tao Kan had planned to thrust Huan Xuan toward the Central Plains but died first.
units.literal: Kan had intended to send Xuan north to serve in the Central Plains when Kan died.

units.zh: 後庾亮為荊州，將謀北伐，以宣為都督沔北前鋒征討軍事、平北將軍、司州刺史、假節，鎮襄陽。
units.en: Yu Liang later governed Jingzhou and aimed north, naming Huan Xuan forward commander beyond the Han, general Who Pacifies the North, inspector of Sizhou with credential staff, stationed at Xiangyang.
units.literal: Later Yu Liang held Jingzhou and planned a northern expedition; he appointed Xuan commander of the forward strike north of the Han, general Who Pacifies the North, Inspector of Sizhou with credential staff, garrisoning Xiangyang.

units.zh: 季龍使騎七千渡沔攻之，亮遣司馬王愆期、輔國將軍毛寶救宣。
units.en: Shi Jilong sent seven thousand riders across the Han; Yu Liang answered with Wang Yanqi and Mao Bao, general Who Supports the State.
units.literal: Jilong sent seven thousand horsemen across the Han to attack him; Liang sent aide Wang Yanqi and general Who Supports the State Mao Bao to rescue Xuan.

units.zh: 賊三面為地窟攻城，宣募精勇，出其不意，殺傷數百，多獲鎧馬，賊解圍退走。
units.en: Enemies tunneled from three faces; Huan Xuan drafted daring troops, ambushed them, killed hundreds, seized armored horses, and broke the siege.
units.literal: The bandits dug tunnels on three sides to storm the city; Xuan recruited crack fighters, struck where they did not expect, killed and wounded several hundred, captured many armored horses, and the bandits lifted the siege and withdrew.

units.zh: 久之，宣遣步騎收南陽諸郡百姓沒賊者八千餘人以歸。
units.en: Later he marched foot and horse to rescue over eight thousand southerners trapped under enemy rule.
units.literal: After a long while Xuan sent infantry and cavalry to recover more than eight thousand commoners of the southern commanderies who had fallen to bandits.

units.zh: 庾翼代亮，欲傾國北討，更以宣為都督司梁雍三州荊州之南陽襄陽新野南鄉四郡軍事、梁州刺史、持節，將軍如故。
units.en: Yu Yi replaced Yu Liang and meant to stake the kingdom on a northern war; he gave Huan Xuan command over Si, Liang, Yong, and four Jiangzhou counties—Nanyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, Nanxiang—plus the inspectorate of Liangzhou while keeping his old general's commission.
units.literal: Yu Yi succeeded Liang and wished to commit the whole realm to a northern campaign; he reassigned Xuan as commander of military affairs over Si, Liang, and Yong and over four Jiangzhou commanderies—Nanyang, Xiangyang, Xinye, and Nanxiang—with concurrent appointment as Inspector of Liangzhou, holding his generalship as before.

units.zh: 以前後功，封竟陵縣男。
units.en: Cumulative merit won him the barony of Jingling county.
units.literal: For successive merits he was enfeoffed as Baron of Jingling County.

units.zh: 宣久在襄陽，綏撫僑舊，甚有稱績。
units.en: Huan Xuan remained years at Xiangyang, steadying native and refugee households alike, and won wide acclaim.
units.literal: Xuan long stayed at Xiangyang, comforting settlers old and new, and earned high praise.

units.zh: 庾翼遷鎮襄陽，令宣進伐石季龍將李羆，軍次丹水，為賊所敗。
units.en: When Yu Yi moved his seat to Xiangyang he told Huan Xuan to strike Shi Jilong's general Li Pi; the column stopped at Danshui and lost to enemy troops.
units.literal: When Yu Yi shifted his headquarters to Xiangyang, he ordered Xuan to advance and attack Shi Jilong's commander Li Pi; the army halted at Danshui and was defeated by bandits.

units.zh: 翼怒，貶宣為建威將軍，使移戍峴山。
units.en: Yu Yi, incensed, stripped Huan Xuan down to general Who Displays Might and reassigned him to guard Mount Xian.
units.literal: Yi was furious, demoted Xuan to general Who Displays Might, and ordered him to shift his garrison to Mount Xian.

units.zh: 宣望實俱喪，兼以老疾，時南蠻校尉王愆期守江陵，以疾求代，翼以宣為鎮南將軍、南郡太守，代愆期。
units.en: Stripped of prestige and vigor and slowed by age and sickness, Huan Xuan faced relief when Wang Yanqi, colonel on the southern frontier, begged out of Jiangling; Yu Yi named Huan Xuan general Who Guards the South and administrator of Nan commandery to succeed him.
units.literal: Xuan had lost both reputation and substance, compounded by age and illness; Colonel Who Subdues the Southern Barbarians Wang Yanqi held Jiangling and requested replacement on grounds of illness, so Yi appointed Xuan general Who Guards the South and Administrator of Nan Commandery in Yanqi's stead.

units.zh: 宣不得志，未之官，發憤卒。
units.en: Huan Xuan never assumed the post, heartsick and furious, and died before taking command.
units.literal: Xuan, frustrated in ambition, never took office and died of bitter resentment.

units.zh: 追贈鎮南將軍。
units.en: The court posthumously promoted him to general Who Guards the South.
units.literal: Posthumously honored as general Who Guards the South.

units.zh: 戎官至新野太守。
units.en: Huan Rong eventually served as administrator of Xinye.
units.literal: Rong rose to the rank of Administrator of Xinye.

units.zh: 族子伊
units.en: His collateral kinsman Huan Yi.
units.literal: Clansman Yi.

units.zh: 伊字叔夏，父景，有當世才幹，仕至侍中、丹陽尹、中領軍、護軍將軍、長社侯，伊有武幹，標悟簡率，為王濛、劉惔所知，頻參諸府軍事，累遷大司馬參軍。
units.en: Huan Yi, courtesy Shuxia, inherited his father Jing's capable service—court posts through marquis of Changshe—and showed martial grit, sharp perception, and blunt simplicity that won Wang Meng and Liu Tan; staff appointments piled up until he served the Grand Marshal.
units.literal: Yi styled Shuxia; his father Jing possessed timely administrative talent and reached Palace Attendant, Administrator of Danyang, Central Army Commander, general Who Guards the Army, and Marquis of Changshe; Yi had martial capacity and was marked by keen insight and straightforward simplicity; Wang Meng and Liu Tan appreciated him; he repeatedly joined headquarters on military affairs and was promoted to aide on the Grand Marshal's staff.

units.zh: 時苻堅強盛，邊鄙多虞，朝議選能距捍疆場者，乃授伊淮南太守。
units.en: Fu Jian's might kept the borders uneasy, so ministers picked Huan Yi to hold the line as administrator of Huainan.
units.literal: At that time Fu Jian was powerful and the frontier bristled with alarms; court deliberation chose someone able to hold the marches and appointed Yi Administrator of Huainan.

units.zh: 以綏禦有方，進督豫州之十二郡揚州之江西五郡軍事、建威將軍、曆陽太守，淮南如故。
units.en: His steady hand on defense earned him command over a dozen Yuzhou counties plus five Yangzhou counties west of the Long River, the generalship Who Displays Might, and the Liyang magistracy while he kept Huainan.
units.literal: Because he soothed and defended effectively, he was advanced to supervise military affairs over twelve commanderies of Yuzhou and five commanderies west of the river in Yangzhou, became general Who Displays Might and Administrator of Liyang, retaining Huainan as before.

units.zh: 與謝玄共破賊別將王鑒、張蠔等，以功封宣城縣子，又進都督豫州諸軍事、西中郎將、豫州刺史。
units.en: With Xie Xuan he crushed Wang Jian, Zhang Hao, and other enemy columns, meriting the viscounty of Xuancheng and later full Yuzhou command as western palace general and inspector.
units.literal: Together with Xie Xuan he defeated the bandits' detached commanders Wang Jian and Zhang Hao and others; for merit he was enfeoffed Viscount of Xuancheng and further promoted commander of all military affairs of Yuzhou, General of the Western Palace Court, and Inspector of Yuzhou.

units.zh: 及苻堅南寇，伊與冠軍將軍謝玄、輔國將軍謝琰俱破堅於肥水，以功封永修縣侯，進號右軍將軍，賜錢百萬，袍表千端。
units.en: At the Fei River he stood with Xie Xuan and Xie Yan to break Fu Jian's southern thrust, earning the marquisate of Yongxiu, the title of general of the Right Army, and lavish gifts of coin and silk.
units.literal: When Fu Jian invaded south, Yi together with Champion general Xie Xuan and general Who Supports the State Xie Yan defeated Jian at the Fei River; for merit he was enfeoffed Marquis of Yongxiu, promoted to general of the Right Army, and granted a million cash and a thousand bolts of robe silk.

units.zh: 伊性謙素，雖有大功，而始終不替。
units.en: Huan Yi stayed humble even after towering deeds and never put on airs.
units.literal: Yi was modest by nature; though he achieved great merit, he never changed.

units.zh: 善音樂，盡一時之妙，為江左第一。
units.en: In musicianship he matched the finest of the age and stood first among talent east of the river.
units.literal: He excelled at music and attained the utmost mastery of his age, ranking first east of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 有蔡邕柯亭笛，常自吹之。
units.en: He kept Cai Yong's flute from Ke Pavilion and often performed on it.
units.literal: He possessed Cai Yong's Ke Pavilion flute and often played it himself.

units.zh: 王徽之赴召京師，泊舟青溪側。
units.en: Summoned to the capital, Wang Huizhi tied up below Green Creek.
units.literal: Wang Huizhi went to the capital on summons and moored his boat beside the Green Creek.

units.zh: 素不與徽之相識。
units.en: Huan Yi had never met Wang Huizhi before.
units.literal: He had never been acquainted with Huizhi.

units.zh: 伊於岸上過，船中客稱伊小字曰：「此桓野王也。」
units.en: As Huan Yi walked the shore a traveler in the boat cried his childhood name: "There goes Wild Lord Huan."
units.literal: Yi passed along the bank; a passenger in the boat called Yi's childhood name and said: "That is Huan the Wild Lord."

units.zh: 徽之便令人謂伊曰：「聞君善吹笛，試為我一奏。」
units.en: Wang Huizhi sent word: "They say your flute is unmatched—play for me."
units.literal: Huizhi then sent someone to tell Yi: "I hear you play the flute well—play a piece for me."

units.zh: 伊是時已貴顯，素聞徽之名，便下車，踞胡床，為作三調，弄畢，便上車去，客主不交一言。
units.en: Already a great man who respected Wang Huizhi's fame, Huan Yi still dismounted, spread a camp stool, ripped through three pieces, remounted, and rode off—not a sentence passed between them.
units.literal: Though Yi was already eminent and had long heard Huizhi's name, he stepped from his carriage, sat cross-legged on a folding stool, performed three tunes, finished his improvisation, boarded his carriage and left—host and guest exchanged not a word.

units.zh: 時謝安女婿王國寶專利無檢行，安惡其為人，每抑制之。
units.en: Wang Guobao, Xie An's son-in-law, grew rich through shameless grabs; Xie An despised him and checked him at every turn.
units.literal: At that time Xie An's son-in-law Wang Guobao behaved graspingly without restraint; An detested his character and constantly restrained him.

units.zh: 及孝武末年，嗜酒好內，而會稽王道子昏ＪＴ尤甚，惟狎昵諂邪，於是國寶讒諛之計稍行於主相之間。
units.en: Late in Emperor Xiaowu's reign the throne drowned in wine and harem sport while Prince Wang Daozi of Kuaiji slid deeper into folly and vice, cuddling only sneaks and toadies—room for Wang Guobao's whisper campaigns between emperor and chief minister.
units.literal: By the late Xiaowu reign the emperor indulged wine and inner chambers, while Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi sank deeper into befuddled dissipation; he favored only flatterers and sycophants, so Guobao's slanderous schemes gradually operated between sovereign and chief minister.

units.zh: 而好利險詖之徒，以安功名盛極，而構會之，嫌隙遂成。
units.en: The grasping and crooked, jealous of Xie An's zenith, spun plots until sovereign and minister eyed each other with mistrust.
units.literal: Men greedy and treacherous, seeing An's fame at its peak, engineered suspicion against him, and estrangement took shape.

units.zh: 帝召伊飲宴，安侍坐。
units.en: The emperor called Huan Yi to drink while Xie An sat with them.
units.literal: The emperor summoned Yi to a drinking banquet with An in attendance.

units.zh: 帝命伊吹笛。
units.en: He told Huan Yi to sound the flute.
units.literal: The emperor ordered Yi to play the flute.

units.zh: 伊神色無迕，即吹為一弄，乃放笛云：「臣於箏分乃不及笛，然自足以韻合歌管，請以箏歌，並請一吹笛人。」
units.en: Huan Yi betrayed no unease, delivered a full set, laid the flute aside, and said: "My zheng falls short of my piping, yet it can carry a song—let me sing with it and borrow another blower."
units.literal: Yi showed no awkwardness, played one suite at once, then set down the flute and said: "In skill on the zheng I do not match the flute, yet it is enough to harmonize with song and pipes—allow me to sing to the zheng and also request one flutist."

units.zh: 帝善其調達，乃敕禦妓奏笛。
units.en: The emperor admired his poise and told court musicians to answer on flute.
units.literal: The emperor praised his tact and ordered palace musicians to play flute.

units.zh: 伊又云：「禦府人於臣必自不合，臣有一奴，善相便串。」
units.en: He added: "Your palace band would clash with me—I keep a servant who blends well."
units.literal: Yi added: "Palace performers would surely not suit me; I have a slave skilled at accompanying."

units.zh: 帝彌賞其放率，乃許召之。
units.en: Delighted by his blunt honesty, the emperor let him call the man in.
units.literal: The emperor all the more admired his candor and permitted summoning him.

units.zh: 奴既吹笛，伊便撫箏而歌《怨詩》曰：「為君既不易，為臣良獨難。
units.en: After the slave piped, Huan Yi struck the zheng and sang 《Song of Resentment》: "Serving as lord is never easy; serving as minister is harder still.
units.literal: When the slave had played the flute, Yi plucked the zheng and sang 《Song of Resentment》: "To be your lord is already hard; to be your minister is harder still.

units.zh: 忠信事不顯，乃有見疑患。
units.en: Loyal faith wins no spotlight—only doubt crowds in.
units.literal: Loyalty goes unseen; then comes suspicion's plague.

units.zh: 周旦佐文武，《金縢》功不刊。
units.en: The Zhou dukes steadied King Wen and King Wu; 《Metal-bound Coffer》 preserves their uncarved merit.
units.literal: The Zhou dukes aided kings Wen and Wu; 《Metal-bound Coffer》 records deeds never to be erased.

units.zh: 推心輔王政，二叔反流言。」
units.en: They lent whole hearts to the throne—yet the two rival uncles aired poisonous gossip."
units.literal: With open hearts they aided the royal government; the two uncles spread slanderous rumor."

units.zh: 聲節慷慨，俯仰可觀。
units.en: Every phrase rang with fierce cadence; his bearing matched the words.
units.literal: His tones were stirring in rhythm and gesture.

units.zh: 安泣下沾衿，乃越席而就之，捋其須曰：「使君于此不凡！」
units.en: Xie An wept until his collar ran wet, slid across the mat, tugged Huan Yi's beard, and cried: "No ordinary soul could do this!"
units.literal: An wept until his collar was soaked; crossing his mat he approached Yi, stroked his beard and said: "You are no ordinary man in this!"

units.zh: 帝甚有愧色。
units.en: The emperor flushed with shame.
units.literal: The emperor looked deeply ashamed.

units.zh: 伊在州十年，綏撫荒雜，甚得物情。
units.en: Huan Yi governed a decade, steadying a battered, mixed populace and earning deep affection.
units.literal: Yi held the province ten years, comforting a mixed and desolate population, and won great sympathy.

units.zh: 桓沖卒，遷都督江州荊州十郡豫州四郡軍事、江州刺史，將軍如故，假節。
units.en: After Huan Chong's death he took joint command of Jiangzhou, Jingzhou, and four Yuzhou counties, kept his general's commission, bore the credential staff, and became inspector of Jiangzhou.
units.literal: When Huan Chong died, Yi was transferred to commander of military affairs over ten commanderies of Jiangzhou and Jingzhou and four of Yuzhou, Inspector of Jiangzhou, general as before, with credential staff.

units.zh: 伊到鎮，以邊境無虞，宜以寬恤為務，乃上疏以江州虛秏，加連歲不登，今餘戶有五萬六千，宜併合小縣，除諸郡逋米，移州還鎮豫章。
units.en: On arrival he judged the border calm and pushed lenient relief, arguing that Jiangzhou was bled white by serial crop failure—only fifty-six thousand households remained—so petty counties should merge, grain arrears should vanish, and the provincial seat should return to Yuzhang.
units.literal: When Yi reached his post, deeming the frontier quiet and relief the proper task, he memorialized that Jiangzhou was drained and harvests had failed year after year; the remaining households numbered fifty-six thousand and ought to merge petty counties, remit overdue grain owed commanderies, and move the provincial seat back to Yuzhang.

units.zh: 詔令移州尋陽，其餘皆聽之。
units.en: The throne shifted the provincial seat to Xunyang and granted the other requests.
units.literal: An edict ordered the province shifted to Xunyang; the rest was approved.

units.zh: 伊隨宜拯撫，百姓賴焉。
units.en: He patched wounds wherever needed and the people leaned on him.
units.literal: Yi aided and settled as circumstances demanded; the people relied on him.

units.zh: 在任累年，徵拜護軍將軍。
units.en: Years later the court recalled him as general Who Guards the Army.
units.literal: After many years in office he was summoned as general Who Guards the Army.

units.zh: 以右軍府千人自隨，配護軍府。
units.en: He transferred the thousand household guards of the Right Army headquarters into the Guard Army staff.
units.literal: He brought the thousand men of the Right Army headquarters with him to staff the Guard Army office.

units.zh: 卒官。
units.en: He died still holding office.
units.literal: He died in office.

units.zh: 贈右將軍，加散騎常侍，諡曰烈。
units.en: They posthumously named him general of the right, added ordinary attendant status, and gave the posthumous epithet Martyr.
units.literal: Posthumously honored as general of the Right with additional appointment as palace attendant cavalier in ordinary attendance; posthumous title Martyr.

units.zh: 初，伊有馬步鎧六百領，豫為表，令死乃上之。
units.en: Early on Huan Yi stockpiled six hundred suits of horse and foot mail and drafted a memorial to file only after his death.
units.literal: At first Yi had six hundred suits of horse and foot armor; he prepared a memorial in advance ordering it submitted only after his death.

units.zh: 表曰：「臣過蒙殊寵，受任西籓。
units.en: It read: "Beyond merit I was favored with the western frontier.
units.literal: The memorial said: "I have received undue favor and hold the western march.

units.zh: 淮南之捷，逆兵奔北，人馬器鎧，隨處放散。
units.en: When Huainan fell the foe fled north, littering the roads with men, mounts, and harness.
units.literal: At the Huainan victory the rebel army fled north; men, horses, and armor were scattered everywhere.

units.zh: 于時收拾敗破，不足貫連。
units.en: What we salvaged then was scraps—barely enough to equip a line.
units.literal: At that time we gathered broken gear—too little to string together.

units.zh: 比年營繕，並已修整。
units.en: Workshops since patched every piece.
units.literal: Over the years camp workshops have restored it all.

units.zh: 今六合雖一，餘燼未滅，臣不以朽邁，猶欲輸效力命，仰報皇恩。
units.en: The realm looks whole yet sparks remain; though I am aged and frail I hoped still to spend my strength repaying the throne.
units.literal: Though the realm is now united, embers of rebellion remain; though I am old and worn, I still wished to offer my strength and repay imperial grace.

units.zh: 此志永絕，銜恨泉壤。
units.en: That dream is ended—I carry regret into the grave.
units.literal: That resolve is ended forever; I bear regret unto the yellow springs.

units.zh: 謹奉輸馬具裝百具、步鎧五百領，並在尋陽，請勒所屬領受。」
units.en: I deliver one hundred caparisoned mounts and five hundred suits of infantry armor held at Xunyang—please tell the bureaus to take charge."
units.literal: I respectfully present one hundred fully barded horses, five hundred suits of foot armor, stored at Xunyang—order the relevant offices to receive them."

units.zh: 詔曰：「伊忠誠不遂，益以傷懷，仍受其所上之鎧。」
units.en: The edict answered: "Huan Yi's devotion cut short deepens our grief—take the armor he offers."
units.literal: The edict said: "Yi's loyalty unfulfilled wounds us the more; accept the armor he presents."

units.zh: 子肅之嗣。
units.en: His heir Suzhi succeeded.
units.literal: His son Suzhi inherited.

units.zh: 卒，子陵嗣。
units.en: When Suzhi died, Ling inherited the title.
units.literal: When he died, his son Ling inherited.

units.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
units.en: The Liu Song takeover erased the fief.
units.literal: When Song received the abdication, the principality was abolished.

units.zh: 伊弟不才，亦有將略。
units.en: His younger brother Huan Bucai too carried tactical skill.
units.literal: Yi's younger brother Bucai also possessed strategic talent.

units.zh: 討孫恩，至冠軍將軍。
units.en: Campaigning against Sun En he rose to champion general.
units.literal: He campaigned against Sun En and reached the rank of Champion general.

units.zh: 朱伺，字仲文，安陸人。
units.en: Zhu Si, courtesy Zhongwen, came from Anlu.
units.literal: Zhu Si, styled Zhongwen, was a man of Anlu.

units.zh: 少為吳牙門將陶丹給使。
units.en: Young, he was a runner for Tao Dan, Wu's camp commander.
units.literal: In youth he served as orderly for Wu's garrison commander Tao Dan.

units.zh: 吳平，內徙江夏。
units.en: Eastern Wu's fall brought him resettled in Jiangxia.
units.literal: When Wu was pacified, he was moved inland to Jiangxia.

units.zh: 伺有武勇，而訥口，不知書，為郡將督，見鄉里士大夫，揖稱名而已。
units.en: Brave but halting and unread, he served as county captain and only bowed and announced his name before local scholars.
units.literal: Si was martially brave but tongue-tied and illiterate; as commandery captain he merely bowed and spoke his name when meeting local gentry.

units.zh: 及為將，遂以謙恭稱。
units.en: Once promoted to general he won praise for humility.
units.literal: Once he became a commander, he was praised for modesty.

units.zh: 張昌之逆，太守弓欽走灄口，伺與同輩郴寶、布興合眾討之，不克，乃與欽奔武昌。
units.en: When Zhang Chang rose, Administrator Gong Qin bolted to Hankou; Zhu Si with Chen Bao and Bu Xing tried to crush the revolt, failed, and ran with Gong Qin to Wuchang.
units.literal: During Zhang Chang's rebellion the Administrator Gong Qin fled to Hankou; Si joined peers Chen Bao and Bu Xing to raise troops against him; failing, he fled with Qin to Wuchang.

units.zh: 後更率部黨攻滅之。
units.en: Later he rallied his band and wiped Zhang Chang out.
units.literal: Later he led his clique to attack and destroy Zhang Chang.

units.zh: 轉騎部曲督，加綏夷都尉。
units.en: They moved him to cavalry corps command and named him colonel Who Pacifies the Yi.
units.literal: He was transferred to cavalry corps commander with additional appointment as colonel Who Pacifies the Yi.

units.zh: 伺部曲等以諸縣附昌，惟本部唱義討逆，逆順有嫌，求別立縣，因此遂割安陸東界為灄陽縣而貫焉。
units.en: His soldiers noted neighbors had backed Zhang Chang while they alone struck the traitor—awkward living among former allies—so they won a new county carved from eastern Anlu called Sheyang.
units.literal: Si's troops noted that various counties had sided with Zhang Chang while only their corps had raised the righteous cause against the rebel—the awkwardness of opposing former neighbors led them to ask for a separate county; accordingly the eastern border of Anlu was carved off as Sheyang County and attached to them.

units.zh: 其後陳敏作亂，陶侃時鎮江夏，以伺能水戰，曉作舟艦，乃遣作大艦，署為左甄，據江口，摧破敏前鋒。
units.en: Chen Min's revolt found Tao Kan defending Jiangxia; knowing Zhu Si mastered river war and shipwrighting, Kan built a great hull, posted him on the left horn at the estuary, and shattered Chen Min's van.
units.literal: Later Chen Min rebelled; Tao Kan then held Jiangxia and, knowing Si excelled at river combat and understood building ships, sent him to construct a great vessel, appointed him left horn of the formation, held the river mouth, and shattered Chen Min's vanguard.

units.zh: 敏弟恢稱荊州刺史，在武昌，侃率伺及諸軍進討，破之。
units.en: Chen Min's brother Hui claimed Jingzhou from Wuchang until Tao Kan marched Zhu Si and the army to break him.
units.literal: Min's younger brother Hui styled himself Inspector of Jingzhou at Wuchang; Kan led Si and the host to attack and defeated him.

units.zh: 敏、恢既平，伺以功封亭侯，領騎督。
units.en: Once both brothers fell Zhu Si earned a village marquisate and cavalry command.
units.literal: After Min and Hui were pacified, Si was enfeoffed Village Marquis for merit and became cavalry commander.

units.zh: 時西陽夷賊抄掠江夏，太守楊瑉每請督將議距賊之計，伺獨不言。
units.en: Xiyang tribesmen harried Jiangxia while Administrator Yang Min endlessly convened officers—Zhu Si alone stayed silent.
units.literal: At that time Xiyang Yi bandits raided Jiangxia; Administrator Yang Min constantly convened commanders to discuss resisting them; alone Si said nothing.

units.zh: 瑉曰：「朱將軍何以不言？」
units.en: Yang Min asked: "Why nothing from General Zhu?"
units.literal: Min said: "Why does General Zhu not speak?"

units.zh: 伺答曰：「諸人以舌擊賊，伺惟以力耳。」
units.en: Zhu Si answered: "They fight with words; I fight with steel."
units.literal: Si replied: "They all strike bandits with tongues; I only strike with strength."

units.zh: 瑉又問：「將軍前後擊賊，何以每得勝邪？」
units.en: "Then why do you always win?" Yang pressed."
units.literal: Min asked again: "General, when you fight bandits why do you always win?"

units.zh: 伺曰：「兩敵共對，惟當忍之。
units.en: "Because two armies meet and patience decides it.
units.literal: Si said: "When two foes face each other, one must endure.

units.zh: 彼不能忍，我能忍，是以勝耳。」
units.en: They lose patience first; I wait—that is victory."
units.literal: They cannot endure; I can—that is why I win."

units.zh: 瑉大笑。
units.en: Yang Min roared with laughter.
units.literal: Min roared with laughter.

units.zh: 永嘉中，石勒破江夏，伺與楊瑉走夏口。
units.en: Under the Yongjia reign Shi Le smashed Jiangxia; Zhu Si and Yang Min escaped to Xiakou.
units.literal: During Yongjia, Shi Le crushed Jiangxia; Si and Yang Min fled to Xiakou.

units.zh: 及陶侃來戍夏口，伺依之，加明威將軍。
units.en: Tao Kan's arrival at Xiakou drew Zhu Si into his command and the generalship Who Displays Martial Glory.
units.literal: When Tao Kan came to garrison Xiakou, Si attached himself to him and was promoted general Who Displays Martial Glory.

units.zh: 隨侃討杜弢，有殊功，語在侃傳。
units.en: He followed Kan against Du Tao with standout feats recorded in Kan's memoir.
units.literal: He followed Kan against Du Tao with exceptional merit, as related in Kan's biography.

units.zh: 夏口之戰，伺用鐵面自衛，以弩的射賊大帥數人，皆殺之。
units.en: At Xiakou he wore an iron mask, aimed his crossbow, and dropped several enemy captains.
units.literal: At the battle of Xiakou Si wore an iron mask for protection and with crossbow sights shot several enemy chiefs, killing them.

units.zh: 賊挽船上岸，於水邊作陣。
units.en: The raiders dragged boats aground and drew lines along the bank.
units.literal: The bandits towed boats ashore and formed ranks along the water.

units.zh: 伺逐水上下以邀之，箭中其脛，氣色不變。
units.en: Zhu Si prowled the shallows to cut them off; a bolt pierced his shin yet his face stayed calm.
units.literal: Si ranged up and down the water to intercept them; an arrow struck his shin yet his bearing never changed.

units.zh: 諸軍尋至，賊潰，追擊之，皆棄船投水，死者太半。
units.en: Reinforcements arrived, routed them, and drove survivors into the river—more than half drowned.
units.literal: The armies soon arrived; the bandits broke and fled in pursuit; all abandoned boats for the water and more than half died.

units.zh: 賊夜還長沙，伺追蒲圻，不及而反。
units.en: They slipped overnight toward Changsha; Zhu Si chased to Puqi, missed them, and withdrew.
units.literal: The bandits fled by night to Changsha; Si pursued to Puqi but did not catch them and turned back.

units.zh: 加威遠將軍，赤幢曲蓋。
units.en: Promotion followed to general Who Displays Far Might with scarlet banner and curved canopy.
units.literal: He was promoted general Who Displays Far Might with crimson banner and curved canopy.

units.zh: 建興中，陳聲率諸無賴二千餘家斷江抄掠，侃遣伺為督護討聲。
units.en: In Jianxing Chen Sheng stacked two thousand restless families across the river as pirates until Tao Kan sent Zhu Si as protector to crush him.
units.literal: During Jianxing, Chen Sheng led over two thousand rogue households to block the river and plunder; Kan dispatched Si as protector to attack Sheng.

units.zh: 聲眾雖少，伺容之不擊，求遣弟詣侃降，伺外許之。
units.en: Chen Sheng's band was small yet Zhu Si held fire, let him send a brother to sue for peace with Kan, and nodded along.
units.literal: Though Sheng's followers were few, Si tolerated them without striking and requested permission to send his younger brother to Kan to surrender; Si outwardly consented.

units.zh: 及聲去，伺乃遣勁勇要聲弟斬之，潛軍襲聲。
units.en: Once Chen Sheng left, Zhu Si ambushed the brother, took his head, and stole a march on the chief.
units.literal: After Sheng departed, Si sent crack troops to intercept Sheng's brother and behead him, then secretly marched against Sheng.

units.zh: 聲正旦並出祭祀飲食，伺軍入其門方覺。
units.en: New Year's dawn found Chen Sheng's men feasting at sacrifice while Zhu Si burst his gates unnoticed.
units.literal: On New Year's morning Sheng all went out for sacrifice and feasting; Si's troops entered his gate before he noticed.

units.zh: 聲將閻晉、鄭進皆死戰，伺軍人多傷，乃還營。
units.en: Captains Yan Jin and Zheng Jin sold their lives dearly; Zhu Si's troops bled heavy losses and pulled back.
units.literal: Sheng's commanders Yan Jin and Zheng Jin fought to the death; Si's men suffered many wounds and withdrew to camp.

units.zh: 聲東走，保董城。
units.en: Chen Sheng bolted east and dug in at Dong city.
units.literal: Sheng fled east and held Dong City.

units.zh: 伺又率諸軍圍守之，遂重柴繞城，作高櫓，以勁弩下射之，又斷其水道。
units.en: Zhu Si invested the place, ringed it with faggots, raised tall racks, poured crossbow fire downward, and dammed the water.
units.literal: Si again led the host to besiege him, piled heavy firewood around the walls, built lofty towers, shot down with powerful crossbows, and cut his water supply.

units.zh: 城中無水，殺牛飲血。
units.en: Dry wells drove them to butcher cattle and drink blood.
units.literal: With no water inside the city they slaughtered cattle and drank blood.

units.zh: 閻晉，聲婦弟也，乃斬聲首出降。
units.en: Yan Jin, Chen Sheng's brother-in-law, struck off his head and walked out to yield.
units.literal: Yan Jin was Sheng's wife's younger brother; he beheaded Sheng and came out to surrender.

units.zh: 又以平蜀賊襲高之功，加伺廣威將軍，領竟陵內史。
units.en: Breaking Shu raider Xi Gao earned Zhu Si the generalship Who Displays Broad Might and the interior secretaryship of Jingling.
units.literal: For merit in pacifying Shu bandit Xi Gao, Si was promoted general Who Displays Broad Might and concurrent Interior Secretary of Jingling.

units.zh: 時王敦欲用從弟暠代侃為荊州，侃故將鄭攀、馬俊等乞侃於敦，敦不許。
units.en: Wang Dun meant to swap Tao Kan for cousin Wang Gao as Jingzhou inspector; Kan's veterans Zheng Pan and Ma Jun pleaded in vain.
units.literal: At that time Wang Dun wished to install his cousin Gao to replace Kan as Inspector of Jingzhou; Kan's old officers Zheng Pan and Ma Jun begged Dun on Kan's behalf but Dun refused.

units.zh: 攀等以侃始滅大賊，人皆樂附，又以暠忌戾難事，謀共距之。
units.en: They argued Tao Kan had just crushed a major foe and kept popular loyalty, whereas Wang Gao was jealous and vicious—so they conspired to resist.
units.literal: Pan and others noted Kan had just destroyed a great bandit and men gladly followed him, also that Gao was jealous and cruel and hard to serve; they plotted jointly to resist.

units.zh: 遂屯結溳口，遣使告伺。
units.en: They rallied at Hankou and messaged Zhu Si.
units.literal: They massed at Hankou and sent envoys to inform Si.

units.zh: 伺外許之，而稱疾不赴。
units.en: Zhu Si agreed in words but pleaded sickness and stayed away.
units.literal: Si outwardly consented but pleaded illness and did not go.

units.zh: 攀等遂進距暠。
units.en: Zheng Pan and company then marched against Wang Gao.
units.literal: Pan and others therefore advanced to oppose Gao.

units.zh: 既而士眾疑阻，復散還橫桑口，欲入杜曾。
units.en: Morale collapsed: the host melted away toward Hengsangkou hoping to throw in with Du Zeng.
units.literal: Presently the troops hesitated and broke apart, scattered back to Hengsangkou, and intended to join Du Zeng.

units.zh: 時朱軌、趙誘、李桓率眾將擊之，攀等懼誅，以司馬孫景造謀距暠，因斬之，降軌等。
units.en: Zhu Gui, Zhao You, and Li Huan threw weight against them; fearing the headsman, Zheng Pan blamed staff officer Sun Jing for opposing Wang Gao, cut him down, and yielded to Zhu Gui.
