units.literal: At that time Zhu Gui, Zhao You, and Li Huan led troops to strike them; Pan and others feared execution and, claiming Marshal Sun Jing had plotted resistance against Gao, beheaded him and surrendered to Gui and company.

units.zh: 廙將西出，遣長史劉浚留鎮揚口壘。
units.en: Preparing a western advance, Wang Yi left chief clerk Liu Jun to guard the Yangkou stockade.
units.literal: Wang Yi was about to march west and dispatched Chief Clerk Liu Jun to remain and hold the rampart at Yangkou.

units.zh: 時杜曾會請討第五猗於襄陽，伺謂廙曰：「曾是猾賊，外示西還，以疑眾心，欲誘引官軍使西，然後兼道襲揚口耳。
units.en: Du Zeng volunteered to strike Di Wuyi at Xiangyang; Zhu Si warned Wang Yi: "Du Zeng is cunning—his westward show is bait to split our minds and lure the army away before he races down on Yangkou.
units.literal: At that time Du Zeng had offered to attack Di Wuyi at Xiangyang; Si said to Wang Yi: "Zeng is a slippery rogue who feigns heading west to unsettle our ranks—he means to drag imperial troops westward, then double back and hit Yangkou along main and side roads.

units.zh: 宜大部分，未可便西。」
units.en: Hold the main body ready—do not march west on impulse."
units.literal: You ought to keep the bulk of the host massed; you must not hurry west yet."

units.zh: 廙性矜厲自用，兼以伺老怯難信，遂西行。
units.en: Wang Yi, rigid and sure of himself, discounted Zhu Si as a fearful old man and pushed west anyway.
units.literal: Wang Yi was harsh, proud, and self-willed; he also thought Si old, timid, and untrustworthy, and therefore marched west.

units.zh: 曾等果馳還。
units.en: Du Zeng wheeled his riders home exactly as predicted.
units.literal: Zeng and others indeed galloped back.

units.zh: 廙乃遣伺歸，裁至壘，即為曾等所圍。
units.en: Wang Yi recalled Zhu Si, who had scarcely reached the fort before Du Zeng ringed it.
units.literal: Wang Yi then sent Si back; barely reaching the fort, Si was surrounded by Zeng and company.

units.zh: 劉浚以壘北門危，欲令伺守之。
units.en: Liu Jun saw the north gate as the weak point and wanted Zhu Si there.
units.literal: Liu Jun deemed the north gate dangerous and wished to assign Si to defend it.

units.zh: 或說浚云：「伺與鄭攀同者。」
units.en: A whisperer told Liu Jun: "Zhu Si marched with Zheng Pan."
units.literal: Someone advised Jun: "Si is of the same party as Zheng Pan."

units.zh: 乃轉守南門。
units.en: So Zhu Si was posted to the south gate instead.
units.literal: So he was shifted to guard the south gate.

units.zh: 賊知之，攻其北門。
units.en: The enemy learned the switch and stormed the north wall.
units.literal: The bandits learned of it and assaulted the north gate.

units.zh: 時鄭攀党馬俊等亦來攻壘，俊妻子先在壘內，或請皮其面以示之。
units.en: Ma Jun, still tied to Zheng Pan, joined the assault; Liu Jun's family sat inside, and voices called for mutilating them to break his nerve.
units.literal: At that time Zheng Pan's partisan Ma Jun and others also came to attack the fort; Jun's wife and children were already inside the rampart, and some urged flaying their faces to display to him.

units.zh: 伺曰：「殺其妻子，未能解圍，但益其怒耳。」
units.en: Zhu Si answered: "Murdering kin will not open the walls—only fan his fury."
units.literal: Si said: "Killing his wife and children would not lift the siege—it would only deepen his rage."

units.zh: 乃止。
units.en: They dropped the idea.
units.literal: So they desisted.

units.zh: 伺常所調弩忽噤不發，伺甚惡之。
units.en: Zhu Si's favorite crossbow froze silent—an ill sign he loathed.
units.literal: The crossbow Si regularly adjusted suddenly jammed and would not shoot; Si took this as a dire omen.

units.zh: 及賊攻陷北門，伺被傷退入船。
units.en: The north gate fell; Zhu Si, bleeding, fell back aboard ship.
units.literal: When the bandits breached the north gate, Si was wounded and withdrew into a boat.

units.zh: 初，浚開諸船底，以木掩之，名為船械。
units.en: Liu Jun had bored hull plugs and masked them with boards—his so-called boat traps.
units.literal: At first Jun had opened the bottoms of all boats and covered them with planks, calling them "boat traps."

units.zh: 伺既入，賊舉鋋摘伺，伺逆接得鋋，反以摘賊。
units.en: Once aboard they thrust boat-hooks at Zhu Si; he caught the shaft and hooked them in return.
units.literal: Once Si had entered, the bandits raised spears to hook him; Si caught the spear point and turned it back against them.

units.zh: 賊走上船屋，大喚云：「賊帥在此！」
units.en: They scrambled to the deckhouse yelling: "The rebel chief is here!"
units.literal: The bandits fled onto the cabin roof and shouted: "The bandit chief is here!"

units.zh: 伺從船底沈行五十步，乃免。
units.en: Zhu Si slipped underwater fifty paces along the keel and broke free.
units.literal: Si submerged along the hull for fifty paces and escaped.

units.zh: 遇醫療，創小差。
units.en: Surgeons dressed him and the gashes began to close.
units.literal: He met doctors; his wounds began to heal.

units.zh: 杜曾遣說伺云：「馬俊等感卿恩，妻孥得活。
units.en: Du Zeng's envoy wheedled: "Ma Jun owes you every breath his family draws.
units.literal: Du Zeng sent someone to persuade Si: "Ma Jun and others are grateful for your kindness—his wife and children lived because of you.

units.zh: 盡以卿家外內百口付俊，俊已盡心收視，卿可來也。」
units.en: He guards a hundred of your kin—every soul—and tends them honestly; join us."
units.literal: He has placed every mouth—inside and outside—of your household in Jun's care; Jun has sheltered them faithfully—you may come over."

units.zh: 伺答曰：「賊無白首者，今吾年六十餘，不能復與卿作賊。
units.en: Zhu Si replied: "Rebels never see white hair; I am past sixty and will not ride with thieves.
units.literal: Si answered: "Bandits never die of old age; I am over sixty and will not turn bandit again for you.

units.zh: 吾死，當歸南，妻子付汝。」
units.en: When I fall, send my bones south—keep wife and children if you must."
units.literal: When I die, I shall return south; my wife and children are yours to keep."

units.zh: 乃還甑山。
units.en: He withdrew to Mount Zeng.
units.literal: So he returned to Zeng Mountain.

units.zh: 時王暠與李桓、杜曾相持，累戰甑山下。
units.en: Wang Gao, Li Huan, and Du Zeng traded blows for days beneath Mount Zeng.
units.literal: At that time Wang Gao locked horns with Li Huan and Du Zeng, fighting repeatedly below Mount Zeng.

units.zh: 軍士數驚喚云：「賊欲至！」
units.en: Men shrieked night and day: "Here they come!"
units.literal: Soldiers kept screaming: "The bandits are coming!"

units.zh: 伺驚創而卒。
units.en: The alarm tore Zhu Si's wound open and killed him.
units.literal: Si started at the wound and died.

units.zh: 因葬甑山。
units.en: They buried him on Mount Zeng.
units.literal: He was therefore buried on Mount Zeng.

units.zh: 毛寶，字碩真，滎陽陽武人也。
units.en: Mao Bao, courtesy Shuozhen, hailed from Yangwu in Yingyang commandery.
units.literal: Mao Bao, styled Shuozhen, was a man of Yangwu in Yingyang.

units.zh: 王敦以為臨湘令。
units.en: Wang Dun named him magistrate of Linxiang.
units.literal: Wang Dun appointed him magistrate of Linxiang.

units.zh: 敦卒，為溫嶠平南參軍。
units.en: After Wang Dun's death he joined Wen Qiao as aide under the general Who Pacifies the South.
units.literal: When Dun died, he became an aide on Wen Qiao's staff as general Who Pacifies the South.

units.zh: 蘇峻作逆，嶠將赴難，而征西將軍陶侃懷疑不從。
units.en: Su Jun's revolt drew Wen Qiao toward the capital while Tao Kan, general Who Conquers the West, hung back in doubt.
units.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, Qiao prepared to march to the rescue, but general Who Conquers the West Tao Kan hesitated and would not follow.

units.zh: 嶠屢說不能回，更遣使順侃意曰：「仁公且守，僕宜先下。」
units.en: Wen Qiao's pleas failed, so he couched a letter to stroke Kan's pride: "Stay put, my lord—I will move downstream first."
units.literal: Qiao argued repeatedly without swaying him and finally sent an envoy phrased to suit Kan: "My lord, hold your ground awhile—I should descend first."

units.zh: 遣信已二日，會寶別使還，聞之，說嶠曰：「凡舉大事，當與天下共同，眾克在和，不聞有異。
units.en: Two days after the courier left, Mao Bao's own rider returned; hearing the plan, he told Wen Qiao: "Great ventures need unity—harmony wins wars; nobody conquers by sowing mistrust.
units.literal: The messenger had been gone two days when Bao's separate envoy returned; hearing this, he told Qiao: "Whenever one raises a great affair one must act with the realm at one's side—victory rests in harmony; one never hears of success through division.

units.zh: 假令可疑，猶當外示不覺，況自作疑耶！
units.en: Even if doubt were fair, feign trust—never manufacture suspicion yourself!
units.literal: Even if suspicion were warranted, one should outwardly show no sign—how much less stir doubt oneself!

units.zh: 便宜急追信，改舊書，說必應俱征。
units.en: Chase that rider, rewrite the letter, and swear you march as one.
units.literal: Best hurry after that messenger, revise the former letter, and declare you will surely campaign together.

units.zh: 若不及前信，宜更遣使。」
units.en: If you cannot catch him, dispatch a fresh messenger."
units.literal: If you cannot overtake the earlier courier, send another envoy."

units.zh: 嶠意悟，即追信改書，侃果共征峻。
units.en: Wen Qiao saw it, recalled the rider, revised the note, and Tao Kan agreed to strike Su Jun.
units.literal: Qiao grasped the point, immediately pursued the courier and altered the letter; Kan indeed joined the expedition against Jun.

units.zh: 寶領千人為嶠前鋒，俱次茄子浦。
units.en: Mao Bao took a thousand men as Wen Qiao's van and camped at Eggplant Ford.
units.literal: Bao led a thousand men as Qiao's vanguard; both halted at Eggplant Ford.

units.zh: 初，嶠以南軍習水，峻軍便步，欲以所長制之，宜令三軍，有上岸者死。
units.en: Wen Qiao bet on southern sailors against Su Jun's infantry and decreed death for anyone who landed.
units.literal: At first Qiao, because southern troops were practiced on water while Jun's army favored foot fighting, wished to leverage strength against weakness and ordered the three armies: whoever went ashore would die.

units.zh: 時蘇峻送米萬斛饋祖約、約遣司馬桓撫等迎之。
units.en: Su Jun shipped ten thousand hu of grain to Zu Yue, who sent Huan Fu and staff to escort it.
units.literal: At that time Su Jun sent ten thousand hu of grain as gift to Zu Yue; Yue dispatched Marshal Huan Fu and others to receive it.

units.zh: 寶告其眾曰：「兵法，軍令有所不從，豈可不上岸邪！」
units.en: Mao Bao harangued his troops: "War allows sensible disobedience—how can we stay dry?"
units.literal: Bao told his men: "In the art of war, orders from headquarters may be disobeyed when circumstances demand—how can we refuse to go ashore!"

units.zh: 乃設變力戰，悉獲其米，虜殺萬計，約用大饑。
units.en: He improvised a landing, seized every sack, slaughtered thousands, and starved Zu Yue.
units.literal: He therefore improvised and fought fiercely, capturing all the grain, killing or capturing on the order of ten thousand, so Yue suffered great famine.

units.zh: 嶠嘉其勳，上為廬江太守。
units.en: Wen Qiao hailed the feat and memorialized him as administrator of Lujiang.
units.literal: Qiao praised his merit and memorialized him as Administrator of Lujiang.

units.zh: 約遣祖煥、桓撫等欲襲湓口，陶侃將自擊之，寶曰：「義軍恃公，公不可動，寶請討之。」
units.en: Zu Yue sent Zu Huan and Huan Fu toward Yikou; Tao Kan wanted to lead in person, but Mao Bao said: "The loyal army pins hope on you—stay; I will go."
units.literal: Yue dispatched Zu Huan and Huan Fu and others intending to raid Yikou; Tao Kan meant to strike them personally; Bao said: "The righteous host looks to you—you cannot move; allow me to attack them."

units.zh: 侃顧謂坐客曰：「此年少言可用也。」
units.en: Tao Kan told his council: "The lad speaks sense."
units.literal: Kan looked around at seated guests and said: "This young man's words can be used."

units.zh: 乃使寶行。
units.en: He gave Mao Bao the sortie.
units.literal: He therefore sent Bao.

units.zh: 先是，桓宣背約，南屯馬頭山，為煥、撫所攻，求救於寶。
units.en: Earlier Huan Xuan split from Zu Yue and held Mount Matou until Zu Huan and Huan Fu besieged him; he cried for Mao Bao.
units.literal: Earlier Huan Xuan had broken with Yue and camped south at Mount Matou; Huan and Fu attacked him, and he begged rescue from Bao.

units.zh: 寶眾以宣本是約黨，疑之。
units.en: Mao Bao's men misliked Huan Xuan as one-time ally of Zu Yue.
units.literal: Bao's troops considered Xuan originally Yue's partisan and doubted him.

units.zh: 宣遣子戎重請，寶即隨戎赴之。
units.en: Huan Xuan sent Huan Rong to insist; Mao Bao marched with him.
units.literal: Xuan sent his son Rong to plead urgently; Bao immediately followed Rong to him.

units.zh: 未至，而賊已與宣戰。
units.en: They arrived late—the enemy was already fighting Huan Xuan.
units.literal: Before they arrived the bandits had already engaged Xuan.

units.zh: 寶軍懸兵少，器杖濫惡，大為煥、撫所破。
units.en: Mao Bao's handful bore rotten gear; Zu Huan and Huan Fu broke them.
units.literal: Bao's army was isolated, few, and poorly armed; Huan and Fu shattered it.

units.zh: 寶中箭，貫髀徹鞍，使人蹋鞍拔箭，血流滿靴，夜奔船所百餘里，望星而行。
units.en: A bolt pinned Mao Bao's thigh through the saddle; a comrade stomped leather to free it while blood filled his boot; he ran a hundred li by starlight toward the fleet.
units.literal: Bao took an arrow through thigh and saddle; he had a man stomp the saddle to draw the shaft; blood filled his boot; he fled by night more than a hundred li to the boats, steering by the stars.

units.zh: 到，先哭戰亡將士，洗瘡訖，夜還救宣。
units.en: He reached camp weeping for the dead, bathed the wound, then doubled back that night for Huan Xuan.
units.literal: Arriving, he first wept for fallen officers, washed his wound, then by night returned to rescue Xuan.

units.zh: 寶至宣營，而煥、撫亦退。
units.en: By the time Mao Bao joined Huan Xuan, Zu Huan and Huan Fu had slipped away.
units.literal: When Bao reached Xuan's camp, Huan and Fu had already withdrawn.

units.zh: 寶進攻祖約，軍次東關，破合肥，尋召歸石頭。
units.en: He pressed Zu Yue, camped at Dong Pass, seized Hefei, then was recalled to Stone Fort.
units.literal: Bao advanced against Zu Yue, halted at Dong Pass, took Hefei, and soon was summoned back to Stone City.

units.zh: 陶侃、溫嶠未能破賊，侃欲率眾南還。
units.en: Tao Kan and Wen Qiao stalled; Kan talked of retreating south.
units.literal: Tao Kan and Wen Qiao could not yet break the bandits; Kan wished to lead the host southward.

units.zh: 寶謂嶠曰：「下官能留之。」
units.en: Mao Bao told Wen Qiao: "I can hold him."
units.literal: Bao told Qiao: "Your subordinate can keep him here."

units.zh: 乃往說侃曰：「公本應領蕪湖，為南北勢援，前既已下，勢不可還。
units.en: He visited Tao Kan: "Wuhu should be your pivot between north and south; now that you have descended the river, withdrawal betrays momentum.
units.literal: He went to persuade Kan: "You ought by rights to hold Wuhu as northern and southern hinge; having already come downstream, momentum forbids return.

units.zh: 且軍政有進無退，非直整齊三軍，示眾必死而已，亦謂退無所據，終至滅亡。
units.en: War moves forward, never back—not only to steel the ranks but because retreat means nowhere to stand and certain ruin.
units.literal: Moreover military principle admits advance, not retreat—not merely to stiffen three armies and show certain death, but because retreat leaves nowhere to stand and ends in annihilation.

units.zh: 往者杜弢非不強盛，公竟滅之，何至於峻獨不可破邪！
units.en: Du Tao was fierce—you crushed him—why fear Su Jun alone?
units.literal: Du Tao was not lacking in strength, yet you destroyed him—how can Jun alone be unbreakable!

units.zh: 賊亦畏死，非皆勇健，公可試與寶兵，使上岸斷賊資糧，出其不意，使賊困蹙。
units.en: Rebels dread death no less—loan me men to cut their grain lines by surprise and choke them.
units.literal: Bandits fear death too; not all are fearless heroes—try lending Bao troops to land, sever their supplies, catch them unprepared, and corner them.

units.zh: 若寶不立效，然後公去，人心不恨。」
units.en: If I fail, withdraw then—no one will blame you."
units.literal: If Bao achieves nothing, then my lord may withdraw without bitterness in men's hearts."

units.zh: 侃然之，加寶督護。
units.en: Tao Kan assented and named Mao Bao protector.
units.literal: Kan agreed and added Bao as protector.

units.zh: 寶燒峻句容、湖孰積聚，峻頗乏食，侃遂留不去。
units.en: Mao Bao torched Su Jun's stockpiles at Jurong and Hushu; hunger pinned Su Jun so Tao Kan remained.
units.literal: Bao burned Jun's granaries at Jurong and Hushu; Jun grew short of food, so Kan stayed and did not leave.

units.zh: 峻既死，匡術以苑城降。
units.en: Su Jun's fall brought Kuang Shu's surrender of the park citadel.
units.literal: After Jun died, Kuang Shu surrendered the imperial park city.

units.zh: 侃使寶守南城，鄧嶽守西城。
units.en: Tao Kan set Mao Bao on the south rampart and Deng Yue on the west.
units.literal: Kan ordered Bao to hold the south wall and Deng Yue the west.

units.zh: 賊遣韓晃攻之，寶登城射殺數十人。
units.en: Han Huang stormed the gate; Mao Bao rained bolts and dropped dozens.
units.literal: The bandits sent Han Huang to attack them; Bao mounted the wall and shot dozens dead.

units.zh: 晃問寶曰：「君是毛廬江邪？」
units.en: Han Huang called: "Are you Mao the Lujiang man?"
units.literal: Huang asked Bao: "Are you Mao of Lujiang?"

units.zh: 寶曰：「是。」
units.en: Mao Bao answered: "I am."
units.literal: Bao said: "Yes."

units.zh: 晃曰：「君名壯勇，何不出鬥！」
units.en: "They say you are fierce—step out and fight!"
units.literal: Huang said: "Your name speaks of valor—why not come out and duel!"

units.zh: 寶曰：「君若健將，何不入鬥！」
units.en: "If you are a real champion, climb the wall yourself!"
units.literal: Bao said: "If you are a stalwart general, why not enter the fight!"

units.zh: 晃笑而退。
units.en: Han Huang laughed and backed off.
units.literal: Huang laughed and withdrew.

units.zh: 賊平，封州陵縣開國侯，千六百戶。
units.en: Peace won him founding marquis of Zhouling with sixteen hundred households.
units.literal: When the bandits were pacified, he was enfeoffed Founding Marquis of Zhouling County with sixteen hundred households.

units.zh: 庾亮西鎮，請為輔國將軍、江夏相、督隨義陽二郡，鎮上明。
units.en: Yu Liang's western command took Mao Bao as general Who Supports the State, chancellor of Jiangxia, overseeing Suí and Yiyang, posted at Shangming.
units.literal: When Yu Liang moved west to command, he requested Bao as general Who Supports the State, Chancellor of Jiangxia, supervising Suí and Yiyang commanderies, garrisoning Shangming.

units.zh: 又進南中郎。
units.en: He rose again to general of the southern palace court.
units.literal: He was further promoted General of the Southern Palace Court.

units.zh: 隨亮討郭默。
units.en: He marched with Yu Liang against Guo Mo.
units.literal: He followed Liang against Guo Mo.

units.zh: 默平，與亮司馬王愆期救桓宣于章山，擊賊將石遇，破之，進征虜將軍。
units.en: Once Guo Mo fell he joined Wang Yanqi to relieve Huan Xuan on Zhang Mountain, broke Shi Yu, and earned the generalship Who Conquers the Caitiffs.
units.literal: After Mo was crushed, together with Liang's aide Wang Yanqi he rescued Huan Xuan at Zhang Mountain, struck bandit commander Shi Yu, defeated him, and was promoted general Who Conquers the Caitiffs.

units.zh: 亮謀北伐，上疏解豫州，請以授寶。
units.en: Yu Liang aimed north and offered Yuzhou to Mao Bao.
units.literal: Liang planned a northern expedition and memorialized to yield Yuzhou, asking it be granted to Bao.

units.zh: 於是詔以寶監揚州之江西諸軍事、豫州刺史，將軍如故，與西陽太守樊峻以萬人守邾城。
units.en: The throne named Mao Bao overseer of Jiangxi military affairs and inspector of Yuzhou at his old rank, pairing him with Fan Jun of Xiyang and ten thousand men at Zhucheng.
units.literal: An edict therefore ordered Bao to supervise all military affairs west of the river in Yangzhou with concurrent appointment as Inspector of Yuzhou, general as before, together with Administrator of Xiyang Fan Jun holding Zhucheng with ten thousand men.

units.zh: 石季龍惡之，乃遣其子鑒與其將夔安、李菟等五萬人來寇，張狢渡二萬騎攻邾城。
units.en: Shi Jilong answered with fifty thousand men under Shi Jian, Kui An, and Li Tu; Zhang Huo splashed twenty thousand cavalry toward Zhucheng.
units.literal: Shi Jilong hated this and sent his son Jian with commanders Kui An, Li Tu, and others—fifty thousand men—to invade; Zhang Huo led twenty thousand horse across the ford against Zhucheng.

units.zh: 寶求救於亮，亮以城固，不時遣軍，城遂陷。
units.en: Mao Bao cried for help; Yu Liang trusted the masonry and tarried until Zhucheng collapsed.
units.literal: Bao begged rescue from Liang; Liang, trusting the walls, did not dispatch troops in time, so the city fell.

units.zh: 寶、峻等率左右突圍出，赴江死者六千人，寶亦溺死。
units.en: Mao Bao, Fan Jun, and escort hacked free; six thousand drowned in the Yangzi—Mao Bao sank with them.
units.literal: Bao, Jun, and others broke out with their guard; six thousand died rushing into the river; Bao also drowned.

units.zh: 亮哭之慟，因發疾，遂薨。
units.en: Yu Liang mourned until grief broke his health and killed him.
units.literal: Liang wept bitterly, fell ill on account of it, and died.

units.zh: 詔曰：「寶之傾敗，宜在貶裁。
units.en: An edict read: "Mao Bao's rout calls for censure.
units.literal: The edict said: "Bao's collapse merits demotion.

units.zh: 然蘇峻之難，致力王室。
units.en: Yet in Su Jun's war he spent himself for the throne.
units.literal: Yet during Su Jun's crisis he exerted himself for the royal house.

units.zh: 今咎其過，故不加贈，祭之可也。」
units.en: Blame his lapse—grant no posthumous rank—but allow offerings."
units.literal: Now, blaming his fault, we add no posthumous honors; sacrifice to him may proceed."

units.zh: 其後公卿言寶有重勳，加死王事，不宜奪爵。
units.en: Ministers later insisted Mao Bao's service outweighed the defeat—stripping his title wronged a martyr.
units.literal: Later ministers argued Bao had heavy merit, died on duty, and ought not lose his nobility.

units.zh: 升平三年，乃下詔復本封。
units.en: In Shengping year three the throne restored his original fief.
units.literal: In the third year of Shengping an edict restored his original enfeoffment.

units.zh: 初，寶在武昌，軍人有于市買得一白龜，長四五寸，養之漸大，放諸江中。
units.en: Once in Wuchang a soldier bought a palm-sized white turtle, raised it to adulthood, and freed it in the Long River.
units.literal: At first, while Bao was at Wuchang, a soldier bought a white turtle four or five inches long in the market, raised it until it grew large, and released it into the river.

units.zh: 邾城之敗，養龜人被鎧持刀，自投于水中，如覺墮一石上，視之，乃先所養白龜，長五六尺，送至東岸，遂得免焉。
units.en: When Zhucheng fell that same man leaped armored into the flood and struck what felt like rock—the giant white turtle he had freed, now six feet long, ferried him east and saved his life.
units.literal: At the fall of Zhucheng the turtle-keeper donned armor, seized a blade, and threw himself into the water; it felt like landing on a stone—looking, it was the former white turtle, five or six chi long, which carried him to the eastern bank so he survived.

units.zh: 寶二子：穆之、安之。
units.en: Mao Bao fathered Muzhi and Anzhi.
units.literal: Bao had two sons: Muzhi and Anzhi.

units.zh: 穆之字憲祖，小字武生，名犯王靖後諱，故行字，後又以桓溫母名憲，乃更稱小字。
units.en: Muzhi took courtesy Xianzu and childhood name Wusheng; taboo on Wang Jing blocked the formal name, so he lived by his courtesy until Huan Wen's mother named Xian forced him back to the childhood name.
units.literal: Muzhi styled Xianzu, childhood name Wusheng; his given name violated the later taboo on Wang Jing, so he used his courtesy name; later because Huan Wen's mother was named Xian he reverted to the childhood name.

units.zh: 穆之果毅有父風，安西將軍庾翼以為參軍。
units.en: Muzhi matched his father's grit; Yu Yi, general Who Pacifies the West, enlisted him.
units.literal: Muzhi was resolute like his father; general Who Pacifies the West Yu Yi took him as aide.

units.zh: 襲爵州陵侯，翼等專威陝西，以子方之為建武將軍，守襄陽。
units.en: He succeeded to Zhouling marquis as Yu Yi dominated Shaanxi and posted son Yu Fangzhi as general Who Displays Might at Xiangyang.
units.literal: He inherited the marquisate of Zhouling; Yi and colleagues wielded power west of the passes and appointed son Fangzhi general Who Displays Martial Might to guard Xiangyang.

units.zh: 方之年少，翼選武將可信杖者為輔弼，乃以穆之為建武司馬。
units.en: Yu Fangzhi's youth moved Yu Yi to pick trustworthy fighters as props and make Muzhi military clerk under the general Who Displays Might.
units.literal: Fangzhi was young; Yi chose reliable warriors to assist him and named Muzhi major clerk under the general Who Displays Might.

units.zh: 俄而翼薨，大將幹瓚、戴羲等作亂，穆之與安西長史江虨、司馬朱燾等共平之。
units.en: Yu Yi's death sparked mutiny from Gan Zan and Dai Xi; Muzhi, chief clerk Jiang Bin, and marshal Zhu Tao crushed it.
units.literal: Soon Yi died; senior generals Gan Zan and Dai Xi rebelled; Muzhi together with chief clerk Jiang Bin and marshal Zhu Tao pacified them.

units.zh: 桓溫代翼，復取為參軍。
units.en: Huan Wen replaced Yu Yi and pulled Mao Muzhi back onto staff.
units.literal: Huan Wen succeeded Yi and again took him as aide.

units.zh: 從溫平蜀，以功賜次子都鄉侯。
units.en: He marched with Huan Wen against Shu and won the lesser heir the village marquisate of Duxiang.
units.literal: He followed Wen to pacify Shu and for merit his second son was granted Village Marquis of Duxiang.

units.zh: 尋除揚威將軍、潁川太守，隨溫平洛，入關。
units.en: Promotion followed to general Who Displays Glory and Yingchuan administrator; he entered Guanzhong on Huan Wen's Luoyang campaign.
units.literal: Soon he was removed to general Who Displays Martial Glory and Administrator of Yingchuan; he followed Wen to pacify Luoyang and entered the passes.

units.zh: 溫將旋師，以謝尚未至，留穆之以二千人衛山陵。
units.en: Huan Wen meant to withdraw before Xie's column arrived, so he detached Mao Muzhi with two thousand soldiers to watch the mausolea.
units.literal: When Wen prepared to wheel the army homeward because Xie had not yet arrived, he left Muzhi with two thousand men to guard the imperial tombs.

units.zh: 升平初，遷督甯州諸軍事、揚威將軍、甯州刺史。
units.en: Early Shengping brought command over Ningzhou armies, the glory generalship, and the Ningzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Shengping era he was transferred to supervise all military affairs of Ningzhou, general Who Displays Martial Glory, and Inspector of Ningzhou.

units.zh: 以桓溫封南郡，徙穆之為建安侯，復為溫太尉參軍。
units.en: Huan Wen's Nan principality shifted Mao Muzhi's fief to Jian'an marquis and returned him to the Grand Commandant's office.
units.literal: Because Huan Wen was enfeoffed Prince of Nan Commandery, Muzhi was shifted to Marquis of Jian'an and again became aide to Wen as Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 加冠軍將軍，以所募兵配之。
units.en: They added champion general and handed him the recruits he had raised.
units.literal: He was additionally named Champion general and the troops he had recruited were assigned to him.

units.zh: 溫伐慕容暐，使穆之監鑿钜野百餘里，引汶會於濟川。
units.en: Against Former Yan he tasked Mao Muzhi with dredging Juye—over a hundred li—to merge the Wen into the Ji.
units.literal: When Wen campaigned against Murong Wei, he had Muzhi supervise cutting a channel more than a hundred li through Juye to draw the Wen River into the Ji River.

units.zh: 及溫焚舟步歸，使穆之督東燕四郡軍事。
units.en: After Huan Wen torched his fleet and walked home, Mao Muzhi governed four Dongyan counties.
units.literal: When Wen burned his boats and marched home on foot, he made Muzhi supervise military affairs of four Dongyan commanderies.

units.zh: 領東燕太守，本官如故。
units.en: He stayed Dongyan administrator while keeping former titles.
units.literal: He held concurrent appointment as Administrator of Dongyan with original offices unchanged.

units.zh: 袁真以壽陽叛，溫將征之。
units.en: Yuan Zhen turned traitor at Shouyang and Huan Wen readied an expedition.
units.literal: Yuan Zhen rebelled at Shouyang; Wen prepared to punish him.

units.zh: 穆之以冠軍領淮南太守，守曆陽。
units.en: Mao Muzhi held champion rank, Huainan magistracy, and the Liyang line.
units.literal: Muzhi as Champion general held concurrent Administrator of Huainan and guarded Liyang.

units.zh: 真平，餘黨分散，乃以穆之督揚州之江西軍事，復領陳郡太守。
units.en: Yuan Zhen's fall scattered diehards; Mao Muzhi took Yangzhou's river-west armies plus Chen commandery again.
units.literal: After Zhen was crushed and remnants scattered, Muzhi was assigned to supervise Jiangxi military affairs in Yangzhou and again held Administrator of Chen Commandery.

units.zh: 俄而徙督揚州之義成荊州五郡雍州之兆軍事、襄陽義成河南三郡太守，將軍如故。
units.en: He moved to command Yicheng plus five Jingzhou counties and Yongzhou's Fengyi circuit—still general while administering Xiangyang, Yicheng, and Henan.
units.literal: Soon he was shifted to supervise military affairs of Yicheng in Yangzhou, five commanderies in Jingzhou, and Fengyi in Yongzhou, where the received graph zhao in the source is emended in most editions to Fengyi, with concurrent appointment as Administrator of Xiangyang, Yicheng, and Henan, general as before.

units.zh: 尋進領梁州刺史。
units.en: Shortly after he added the Liangzhou inspector's seal.
units.literal: Soon he advanced to concurrent Inspector of Liangzhou.

units.zh: 頃之，以疾解職，詔以冠軍征還。
units.en: Illness forced retirement until the court recalled him under champion rank.
units.literal: Before long he resigned on grounds of illness; an edict summoned him back as Champion general.

units.zh: 苻堅別將寇彭城，復以將軍假節、監江北軍事。
units.en: Fu Jian's lieutenant struck Pengcheng; Mao Muzhi returned as credential general overseeing the north bank.
units.literal: When a detached commander of Fu Jian raided Pengcheng, he was again named general with credential staff and supervisor of military affairs north of the Yangzi.

units.zh: 鎮廣陵。
units.en: He held Guangling.
units.literal: He garrisoned Guangling.

units.zh: 遷右將軍、宣城內史、假節，鎮姑孰。
units.en: Promotion brought general of the right, Xuancheng interior secretary, credential staff, and a post at Gushu.
units.literal: He was promoted general of the Right, Interior Secretary of Xuancheng with credential staff, garrisoning Gushu.

units.zh: 穆之以為戍在近畿，無復軍警，不宜加節，上疏辭讓，許之。
units.en: He argued that guarding the inner zone meant no banner was needed; the throne accepted his refusal of the staff.
units.literal: Muzhi considered that the garrison lay near the capital precincts where military alarms no longer arose; it was inappropriate to add credential staff—he memorialized to decline, and permission was granted.

units.zh: 苻堅別將圍襄陽，詔穆之就上明受桓沖節度。
units.en: Fu Jian's siege drew an order for Mao Muzhi to fall under Huan Chong at Shangming.
units.literal: When Fu Jian's detached commander besieged Xiangyang, an edict ordered Muzhi to receive orders from Huan Chong at Shangming.

units.zh: 沖使穆之遊軍沔中。
units.en: Huan Chong told him to patrol the Han basin.
units.literal: Chong ordered Muzhi to roam the army along the Han.

units.zh: 穆之始至，而朱序陷沒，引軍還郡。
units.en: Zhu Xu's capture broke the relief before it landed; Mao Muzhi withdrew to his seat.
units.literal: Hardly had Muzhi arrived when Zhu Xu fell captive; he led the army back to his commandery.

units.zh: 堅眾又寇蜀漢，梁州刺史楊亮、益州刺史周仲孫奔退，沖使穆之督梁州之三郡軍事、右將軍、西蠻校尉、益州刺史、領建平太守、假節，戍巴郡。
units.en: Fu Jian's next thrust hit Shu-Han; Yang Liang and Zhou Zhongsun bolted; Huan Chong piled on Mao Muzhi—three Liangzhou sectors, general of the right, western Yi colonel, Yizhou inspector, Jianping administrator, credential staff, holding Ba.
units.literal: Jian's host next raided Shu and Han; Inspector of Liangzhou Yang Liang and Inspector of Yizhou Zhou Zhongsun fled in retreat; Chong ordered Muzhi to supervise military affairs of three Liangzhou commanderies with concurrent appointments as general of the Right, Colonel Who Subdues the Western Yi, Inspector of Yizhou, Administrator of Jianping with credential staff, garrisoning Ba Commandery.

units.zh: 以子球為梓潼太守。
units.en: He named son Mao Qiu magistrate of Zitong.
units.literal: He appointed his son Qiu Administrator of Zitong.

units.zh: 穆之與球伐堅，至於巴西郡，以糧運乏少，退屯巴東，病卒。
units.en: Father and son reached Ba-Xi but starvation drove them back to Badong, where Mao Muzhi died.
units.literal: Muzhi and Qiu campaigned against Jian as far as Ba-Xi Commandery; grain ran short, so they withdrew to camp at Badong; Muzhi died of illness.

units.zh: 追贈中軍將軍，諡曰烈。
units.en: Posthumous rank hit central army general with the martyr epithet.
units.literal: Posthumously honored as general of the Central Army; posthumous title Martyr.

units.zh: 子珍嗣，位至天門太守。
units.en: Heir Mao Zhen climbed to Tianmen administrator.
units.literal: His son Zhen inherited and rose to Administrator of Tianmen.

units.zh: 珍弟璩、球、璠、瑾、瑗，璩最知名。
units.en: Zhen's brothers Qu, Qiu, Fan, Jin, and Yuan followed—Qu stood tallest in fame.
units.literal: Younger brothers of Zhen were Qu, Qiu, Fan, Jin, and Yuan; Qu was best known.

units.zh: 璩字叔璉。
units.en: Mao Qu took courtesy Shulian.
units.literal: Qu styled Shulian.

units.zh: 弱冠，右將軍桓豁以為參軍。
units.en: Coming of age he entered Huan He's service as aide.
units.literal: At weak-cap age general of the Right Huan He took him as aide.

units.zh: 尋遭父憂，服闕，為謝安衛將軍參軍，除尚書郎。
units.en: Funeral leave followed his father's death; then Xie An's guard office and secretariat appointment.
units.literal: Soon he suffered his father's mourning; when mourning ended he became aide to Xie An's Guard general and was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 安復請為參軍，轉安子琰征虜司馬。
units.en: Xie An pulled him back as aide and shifted him to expedition marshal under Xie Yan.
units.literal: An again requested him as aide and transferred him to be expedition marshal under An's son Yan.

units.zh: 淮肥之役，苻堅迸走，璩與田次之共躡堅，至中陽，不及而歸。
units.en: When Fu Jian ran from Fei River, Mao Qu and Tian Cizi chased him to Zhongyang without closing the kill.
units.literal: At the Huai-Fei campaign, when Fu Jian broke and fled, Qu together with Tian Cizi pursued Jian to Zhongyang but did not catch him and returned.

units.zh: 遷甯朔將軍、淮南太守。
units.en: He rose to northern pacifier and Huainan magistrate.
units.literal: He was promoted general Who Pacifies the North and Administrator of Huainan.

units.zh: 尋補鎮北將軍、譙王恬司馬。
units.en: Next he served Prince Wang Tian of Qiao as marshal under the northern guard general.
units.literal: Soon he filled the post of marshal to Prince of Qiao Wang Tian, general Who Guards the North.

units.zh: 海陵縣界地名青蒲，四面湖澤，皆是菰葑，逃亡所聚，威令不能及。
units.en: Green Reed in Hailing was ringed by lakes choked with mat-grass where outlaws hid beyond the law.
units.literal: Within Hailing County lay a place called Green Reed surrounded on four sides by lakes and marshes—all arrowroot and reed mats—where fugitives gathered beyond the reach of awe and decree.

units.zh: 璩建議率千討人。
units.en: Mao Qu asked for a thousand blades to scour the swamp—scribes likely dropped words after thousand.
units.literal: Qu proposed leading a thousand men to strike them (received text appears abbreviated).

units.zh: 時大旱，璩因放火，菰葑盡然，亡戶窘迫，悉出詣璩自首，近有萬戶，皆以補兵，朝廷嘉之。
units.en: Drought let him burn the reed flats bare; tens of thousands crept out to enlist and the court cheered.
units.literal: At that time severe drought enabled Qu to set fires that burned the mats clear; refugee households, desperate, all presented themselves to Qu to surrender—nearly ten thousand households were drafted as soldiers, and the court praised him.

units.zh: 轉西中郎司馬、龍驤將軍、譙梁二郡內史。
units.en: Moves stacked up: western palace marshal, Soaring Dragon general, interior secretary over Qiao and Liang.
units.literal: He was transferred Western Palace marshal, general Soaring Dragon, and Interior Secretary of Qiao and Liang commanderies.

units.zh: 尋代郭銓為建威將軍、益州刺史。
units.en: He succeeded Guo Quan as mighty-display general and Yizhou inspector.
units.literal: Soon he replaced Guo Quan as general Who Displays Martial Might and Inspector of Yizhou.

units.zh: 安帝初，進征虜將軍。
units.en: Emperor An's opening years brought the caitiff-conquering generalship.
units.literal: At the beginning of Emperor An's reign he was promoted general Who Conquers the Caitiffs.

units.zh: 及桓玄篡位，遣使加璩散騎常侍、左將軍。
units.en: Huan Xuan's coup brought messengers offering Mao Qu left general and ordinary attendant.
units.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne he sent envoys to add Qu ordinary attendant cavalier and general of the Left.

units.zh: 璩執留玄使，不受命。
units.en: Mao Qu locked up the envoy and rejected the patent.
units.literal: Qu detained Xuan's envoy and refused the commission.

units.zh: 玄以桓希為梁州刺史，王異據涪，郭法戍宕渠，師寂戍巴郡，周道子戍白帝以防之。
units.en: Huan Xuan ringed him with Huan Xi in Liangzhou, Wang Yi on the Fu, Guo Fa at Dangqu, Shi Ji in Ba, Zhou Daozi at White Emperor.
units.literal: Xuan appointed Huan Xi Inspector of Liangzhou; Wang Yi held Fu; Guo Fa held Dangqu; Shi Ji held Ba Commandery; Zhou Daozi held Baidicheng to block him.

units.zh: 璩傳檄遠近，列玄罪狀，遣巴東太守柳約之、建平太守羅述、征虜司馬甄季之擊破希等，仍率眾次於白帝。
units.en: Manifestos flew; Liu Yuezhi, Luo Shu, and Zhen Jizhi smashed Huan Xi while Mao Qu anchored at Baidicheng.
units.literal: Qu circulated proclamations far and near listing Xuan's crimes; he dispatched Administrator of Badong Liu Yuezhi, Administrator of Jianping Luo Shu, and expedition marshal Zhen Jizhi to crush Xi and others, then led troops to halt at Baidicheng.

units.zh: 武陵王令曰：「益州刺史毛璩忠誠愨亮，自桓玄萌禍，常思躡其後。
units.en: The Prince of Wuling wrote: "Yizhou inspector Mao Qu proved steadfast—he aimed at Huan Xuan's back from the first.
units.literal: Prince of Wuling's order said: "Inspector of Yizhou Mao Qu is loyal, sincere, and bright; since Huan Xuan bred calamity he has long plotted to tread on Xuan's heels.

units.zh: 今若平殄凶逆，肅清荊郢者，便當即授上流之任。」
units.en: Crush the usurper and cleanse Jing-Ying, and the upper river command is his."
units.literal: If now he levels the traitors and clears Jing and Ying, he shall immediately receive appointment to the upper Yangzi command."

units.zh: 初，璩弟甯州刺史璠卒官，璩兄球孫祐之及參軍費恬以數百人送喪，葬江陵。
units.en: When Mao Fan fell as Ningzhou inspector, grandson Youzhi and Fei Tian convoyed the bier with hundreds to Jiangling.
units.literal: At first Qu's younger brother Fan, Inspector of Ningzhou, died in office; Qu's elder brother Qiu's grandson Youzhi together with aide Fei Tian escorted the funeral with several hundred men and buried him at Jiangling.

units.zh: 會玄敗，謀奔梁州。
units.en: Huan Xuan's rout sent them scheming toward Liangzhou.
units.literal: It happened that Xuan had been defeated and they plotted to flee toward Liangzhou.

units.zh: 璩弟瑾子修之時為玄屯騎校尉，誘玄使入蜀，既而修之與祐之、費恬及漢嘉人馮遷共殺玄。
units.en: Mao Jin's son Xiuzhi, Xuan's cavalry colonel, baited him into Shu, then with Youzhi, Fei Tian, and Feng Qian cut him down.
units.literal: Qu's younger brother Jin's son Xiuzhi was then Xuan's cavalry colonel; he lured Xuan into Shu, after which Xiuzhi together with Youzhi, Fei Tian, and Feng Qian of Hanjia jointly killed Xuan.

units.zh: 約之等聞玄死，進軍到枝復攻沒江陵。
units.en: Liu Yuezhi marched to Zhijiang, struck again, and seized Jiangling on news of Xuan's death.
units.literal: When Yuezhi and company heard Xuan was dead, they advanced to Zhijiang, again attacked, and took Jiangling (received punctuation splits the phrase).

units.zh: 劉毅等還尋陽，約之亦退。
units.en: Liu Yi's retreat to Xunyang pulled Yuezhi back too.
units.literal: When Liu Yi and others returned to Xunyang, Yuezhi also withdrew.

units.zh: 俄而季子、述皆病，約子詣振偽降，因欲襲振而桓振。
units.en: Soon Zhen Jizhi and Luo Shu sickened; Liu Yuezhi's son faked defection to ambush Huan Zhen—who caught the plot.
units.literal: Soon Zhen Jizhi and Luo Shu sickened; Liu Yuezhi's son faked defection to ambush Huan Zhen—who caught the plot.

units.zh: 事泄，被害。
units.en: Word slipped out and he died for it.
units.literal: The affair leaked and he was killed.

units.zh: 約之司馬時延祖、涪陵太守文處茂等撫其餘眾，保涪陵。
units.en: Marshal Shi Yanzu and Wen Chumao of Fuling rallied the remnant behind Fuling's walls.
units.literal: Yuezhi's marshal Shi Yanzu and Administrator of Fuling Wen Chumao then soothed the surviving host and held Fuling.

units.zh: 振遣桓放之為益州，屯西陵。
units.en: Huan Zhen sent Huan Fangzhi toward Yizhou and camped west of the rapids.
units.literal: Zhen dispatched Huan Fangzhi as Inspector of Yizhou and camped at Xiling.

units.zh: 處茂距擊，破之。
units.en: Wen Chumao met him head-on and broke his force.
units.literal: Chumao resisted and struck him, defeating him.

units.zh: 振死，安帝反正，詔曰：「夫貞松標於歲寒，忠臣亮于國危。
units.en: When Huan Zhen died and Emperor An regained the throne, an edict said, "The steadfast pine stands out in bitter cold; the loyal minister shines when the state is in peril.
units.literal: When Zhen died and Emperor An regained the throne, an edict said: "The steadfast pine stands out in bitter cold; the loyal minister shines when the state is in peril.

units.zh: 益州刺史璩體識弘正，誠契義旗，受命偏師，次於近畿，匡翼之勳，實感朕心。
units.en: Mao Qu read the larger loyalty, backed the restoration army, and camped at the capital's elbow—his shelter of the throne touched us.
units.literal: Inspector of Yizhou Qu grasped the great pattern and kept faith with the righteous banner; receiving command of a detached division he halted near the capital precincts—the merit of aiding and sheltering truly moves Us.

units.zh: 可進征西將軍，加散騎常侍，都督益梁秦涼寧五州軍事，行宜都、甯蜀太守。
units.en: Promote him west-conquering general, ordinary attendant, governor of Yi, Liang on the Han, Qin, Hexi Liang, and Ning, acting Yidu and Ningshu magistrate.
units.literal: He may be promoted general Who Conquers the West with additional ordinary attendant cavalier and supervisor of military affairs over Yi, Liang (principal commandery), Qin, Liang (northern frontier), and Ning—five provinces—acting Administrator of Yidu and Ningshu.

units.zh: 文處茂宣贊蕃牧，蒙險夷難，可輔國將軍、西夷校尉、巴西梓潼二郡太守。」
units.en: Wen Chumao, who held the frontier through peril, earns supporting-state general, western Yi colonel, and twin magistracies in Ba and Zitong."
units.literal: Wen Chumao who proclaimed order in the outer marches and braved passes and hardship may become general Who Supports the State, Colonel of the Western Yi, and Administrator of Ba and Zitong commanderies."

units.zh: 又詔西夷校尉瑾為持節、監梁秦二州軍事、征虜將軍、梁秦二州刺史、略陽武都太守。
units.en: Mao Jin kept western Yi colonel but gained credential staff over Liang-Qin, caitiff general, twin inspector, Lüeyang-Wudu administrator.
units.literal: Another edict named Mao Jin, Colonel of the Western Yi, as credential bearer supervising Liang and Qin military affairs, general Who Conquers the Caitiffs, Inspector of Liang and Qin, Administrator of Lüeyang and Wudu.

units.zh: 瑾弟蜀郡太守瑗為輔國將軍、甯州刺史。
units.en: Younger Mao Yuan kept Shu magistracy while gaining supporting general and Ningzhou inspector.
units.literal: Jin's younger brother Yuan, Administrator of Shu Commandery, became general Who Supports the State and Inspector of Ningzhou.

units.zh: 初，璩聞振陷江陵，率眾赴難，使瑾、瑗順外江而下，使參軍譙縱領巴西、梓潼二郡軍下涪水，當與璩軍會于巴郡。
units.en: Learning Jiangling had fallen, Mao Qu marched relief: Jin and Yuan on the main stream, Qiao Zong on the Fu, rendezvousing at Ba.
units.literal: At first, when Qu heard Zhen had taken Jiangling, he led troops to the rescue; he ordered Jin and Yuan down the outer Yangzi while aide Qiao Zong led Ba and Zitong troops down the Fu River to join Qu at Ba Commandery.

units.zh: 蜀人不樂東征，縱因人情思歸，于五城水口反，還襲涪，害瑾，瑾留府長史鄭純之自成都馳使告璩。
units.en: Shu men refused an eastern war; Qiao Zong mutinied at Wucheng, wheeled on Fu, slew Mao Jin, while Zheng Chunzhi raced word to Mao Qu.
units.literal: The people of Shu had no wish to march east; Zong exploited their longing for home and rebelled at Wucheng Ford, doubled back to strike Fu, killed Jin, while Jin's chief clerk Zheng Chunzhi galloped from Chengdu to warn Qu.

units.zh: 璩時在略城，去成都四百里，遣參軍王瓊討反者，相距於廣漢。
units.en: Mao Qu held Lucheng, four hundred li from Chengdu, and sent Wang Qiong to duel Qiao Zong at Guanghan.
units.literal: Qu was then at Lucheng, four hundred li from Chengdu; he dispatched aide Wang Qiong to punish the rebels; they faced each other at Guanghan.

units.zh: 僰道令何林聚黨助縱，而璩下人受縱誘說，遂共害璩及瑗，並子侄之在蜀者，一時殄沒。
units.en: He Lin of Bodao backed Qiao Zong; Mao Qu's soldiers flipped, slaughtering Mao Qu, Mao Yuan, and every kinsman in Shu.
units.literal: Magistrate of Bodao He Lin gathered a band to aid Zong, while Qu's own men succumbed to Zong's blandishments and together murdered Qu and Yuan along with sons and nephews then in Shu—all perished at once.

units.zh: 璩子弘之嗣。
units.en: Son Mao Hongzhi inherited.
units.literal: Qu's son Hongzhi inherited.

units.zh: 義熙中，時延祖為始康太守，上疏訟璩兄弟，於是詔曰：「故益州刺史璩、西夷校尉瑾、蜀郡太守瑗勤王忠烈，事乖慮外。
units.en: During the Yixi era, when Shi Yanzu was administrator of Shikang, he memorialized on behalf of the Qu brothers; an edict said, "The late Inspector of Yizhou Qu, Colonel of the Western Yi Jin, and Administrator of Shu Commandery Yuan served the king with fierce loyalty yet met fate beyond planning.
units.literal: During the Yixi era Shi Yanzu, Administrator of Shikang, memorialized to plead the case of Qu's brothers; an edict therefore said: "The late Inspector of Yizhou Qu, Colonel of the Western Yi Jin, and Administrator of Shu Commandery Yuan served the king with fierce loyalty yet met fate beyond planning.

units.zh: 葬送日近，益懷惻愴，可皆贈先所授官，給錢三十萬、布三百匹。」
units.en: As burial draws near our grief deepens; restore each to his former rank and grant three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth."
units.literal: Their burial draws near and Our grief deepens; restore each to his former rank, grant three hundred thousand cash and three hundred bolts of cloth."

units.zh: 論璩討桓玄功，追封歸鄉公，千五百戶。
units.en: For crushing Huan Xuan Mao Qu won posthumous Duke of Guixiang at fifteen hundred households.
units.literal: Judging Qu's merit in attacking Huan Xuan, posthumous enfeoffment as Duke of Guixiang with fifteen hundred households.

units.zh: 又以祐之斬玄功，封夷道縣侯。
units.en: Youzhi's blade on Xuan earned the Yidao county marquisate.
units.literal: Also for Youzhi's merit in beheading Xuan, enfeoff him Marquis of Yidao County.

units.zh: 自寶至璩三葉，擁旄開國者四人，將帥之家，與尋陽周氏為輩，而人物不及也。
units.en: Three generations from Mao Bao to Mao Qu produced four banner-bearing founders—peer to Xunyang's Zhous if lesser in brilliance.
units.literal: From Bao down to Qu spanned three generations; four men bore credential staffs and founding marquisates—a house of generals ranked with the Zhou clan of Xunyang though its talents fell short.

units.zh: 瑾子修之，頻曆清顯，至右衛將軍，從劉裕平姚泓。
units.en: Mao Xiuzhi climbed clean posts to right guards general and joined Liu Yu against Later Qin.
units.literal: Jin's son Xiuzhi repeatedly rose through pure appointments to general of the Right Guards and followed Liu Yu in pacifying Yao Hong.

units.zh: 後為安西司馬，沒于魏。
units.en: Later western guard marshal, he vanished into Wei captivity.
units.literal: Later he became marshal of the Guard general of the West and was lost to Wei.

units.zh: 安之字仲祖，亦有武幹，累遷撫軍參軍、魏郡太守。
units.en: Mao Anzhi, styled Zhongzu, showed martial talent and rose to army supervisor aide and Wei commandery administrator.
units.literal: Anzhi, courtesy name Zhongzu, likewise had martial ability and was promoted to Army Supervisor Aide and Administrator of Wei Commandery.

units.zh: 簡文輔政，委以爪牙。
units.en: While Emperor Jianwen governed as regent, he kept Anzhi as a trusted enforcer.
units.literal: When Emperor Jianwen assisted the government, he entrusted Anzhi as a trusted enforcer.

units.zh: 及登阼，安之領兵從駕，使止宿宮中。
units.en: On taking the throne he kept Anzhi's troops at court and quartered them inside the palace.
units.literal: When he ascended the throne, Anzhi led troops in attendance on the imperial progress and was ordered to lodge within the palace.

units.zh: 尋拜遊擊將軍。
units.en: Soon he was named mobile corps general.
units.literal: Soon afterward he was appointed Mobile Corps General.

units.zh: 時庾希入京口，朝廷震動，命安之督城門諸軍事。
units.en: When Yu Xi seized Jingkou the court panicked and put Anzhi in charge of the gate garrisons.
units.literal: At that time Yu Xi entered Jingkou and the court was shaken; Anzhi was ordered to supervise all gate-garrison affairs.

units.zh: 孝武即位，妖賊盧悚突入殿廷。
units.en: After Emperor Xiaowu took the throne, the sorcerer Lu Song broke into the hall.
units.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu ascended the throne, the sorcerer-bandit Lu Song burst into the palace hall.

units.zh: 安之聞難，率眾直入雲龍門，手自奮擊。
units.en: Anzhi heard the alarm, charged through the Cloud Dragon Gate, and fought hand to hand.
units.literal: Hearing the crisis, Anzhi led his men straight through the Cloud Dragon Gate and struck with his own hand.

units.zh: 既而左衛將軍殷康、領軍將軍桓秘等至，與安之並力，悚因剿滅。
units.en: Yin Kang, Huan Mi, and others soon joined Anzhi and wiped out Lu Song.
units.literal: Presently General of the Left Guard Yin Kang, Commandant-in-Chief Huan Mi, and others arrived; joining forces with Anzhi, they thereupon exterminated Song.

units.zh: 遷右衛將軍。
units.en: He was promoted to general of the right guard.
units.literal: He was transferred to General of the Right Guard.

units.zh: 定後崩，領將作大匠。
units.en: After Empress Dowager Ding died he headed palace construction.
units.literal: When Empress Dowager Ding died, he took charge as Director of Palace Construction.

units.zh: 卒官。
units.en: He died in office.
units.literal: He died in office.

units.zh: 追贈光祿勳。
units.en: Posthumously he was made superintendent of the imperial household.
units.literal: Posthumously he was granted Superintendent of the Imperial Household.

units.zh: 四子：潭、泰、邃、遁。
units.en: He fathered Tan, Tai, Sui, and Dun.
units.literal: Four sons: Tan, Tai, Sui, and Dun.

units.zh: 潭嗣爵，官至江夏相。
units.en: Eldest Mao Tan took the title and reached Jiangxia chancellor.
units.literal: Tan inherited the nobility and rose to Chancellor of Jiangxia.

units.zh: 泰曆太傅從事中郎、後軍諮議參軍，與邃俱為會稽王父子所昵，乃追論安之討盧悚勳，賜爵平都子，命潭襲爵。
units.en: Mao Tai advised the Grand Tutor and rear army; he and Mao Sui curried Prince Kuaiji's circle until Lu Song's old score won Tai the Pingdu barony while Tan kept the main line.
units.literal: Tai served successively as attendant clerk to the Grand Tutor and advisory aide to the Rear Army; both he and Sui were intimate favorites of Prince of Kuaiji and his son; the court retroactively judged Anzhi's merit against Lu Song and granted Tai the noble rank Baron of Pingdu, ordering Tan to inherit the main marquisate.

units.zh: 元顯嘗宴泰家，既而欲去，泰苦留之曰：「公若遂去，當取公腳。」
units.en: Yuan Xian dined at Mao Tai's then rose to leave; Mao Tai joked he would take his legs if he walked out."
units.literal: Yuan Xian once feasted at Tai's home and afterward wished to leave; Tai urgently detained him saying: "If my lord insists on going I shall take your legs.

units.zh: 元顯大怒，奮衣而出，遂與元顯有隙。
units.en: Yuan Xian stormed out—and enmity opened between him and Mao Tai.
units.literal: Yuan Xian was furious, shook his robes and departed, and thereafter bore ill will toward Tai.

units.zh: 及元顯敗，泰時為冠軍將軍、堂邑太山二郡太守。
units.en: At Yuan Xian's ruin Mao Tai held champion rank over Tangyi and Taishan.
units.literal: When Yuan Xian fell, Tai was then Champion general and concurrent Administrator of Tangyi and Taishan commanderies.

units.zh: 邃為遊擊將軍，遁為太傅主簿，桓玄得志，使泰收元顯，遂於新亭，泰因宿恨，手加毆辱。
units.en: Mao Sui served as roaming striker; Mao Dun clerked the Grand Tutor; Huan Xuan ordered Mao Tai to collar Yuan Xian at Xin Pavilion—where Mao Tai repaid old insults with his fists.
units.literal: Sui was Roaming Strike general; Dun was chief clerk to the Grand Tutor; when Huan Xuan achieved his ambition he ordered Tai to seize Yuan Xian; Tai caught him at Xin Pavilion and, nursing old hatred, personally struck and humiliated him.

units.zh: 俄並為玄所殺，惟遁被徙廣州。
units.en: Huan Xuan soon executed both brothers; only Mao Dun went south in exile.
units.literal: Soon both were killed by Xuan; only Dun was banished to Guangzhou.

units.zh: 義熙初，得還，至宜都太守。
units.en: Yixi's opening saw him home as Yidu magistrate.
units.literal: At the beginning of Yixi he was allowed to return and reached Administrator of Yidu.

units.zh: 德祖，璩宗人也。
units.en: Mao Dezu belonged to Mao Qu's lineage.
units.literal: Dezu was a clansman of Qu.

units.zh: 父祖並沒於賊中。
units.en: Father and grandfather died in rebel chaos.
units.literal: Father and grandfather both perished amid bandits.

units.zh: 德祖兄弟五人，相攜南渡，皆有武幹，荊州刺史劉道規以德祖為建武將軍、始平太守，又徙涪陵太守。
units.en: Five Mao brothers fled south together; Liu Daogui made Mao Dezu mighty-display general, Shiping magistrate, then Fuling.
units.literal: Dezu had five brothers who crossed south together; all possessed martial talent; Inspector of Jingzhou Liu Daogui appointed Dezu general Who Displays Martial Might and Administrator of Shiping, later transferring him to Administrator of Fuling.

units.zh: 盧循之役，道規又以為參軍，伐徐道覆於始興。
units.en: Lu Xun's war brought Mao Dezu back as aide against Xu Daofu at Shixing.
units.literal: During Lu Xun's campaign Daogui again employed him as aide and sent him against Xu Daofu at Shixing.

units.zh: 尋遭母憂。
units.en: Mother's death soon pulled him into mourning.
units.literal: Soon he suffered his mother's mourning.

units.zh: 劉裕伐司馬休之，版補太尉參軍、義陽太守，賜爵遷陵縣侯，轉南陽太守，從劉裕伐姚泓，頻攻滎陽、扶風、南安、馮詡數郡，所在克捷。
units.en: Liu Yu's march on Sima Xiuzhi drafted Mao Dezu as Grand Commandant aide and Yiyang magistrate with Qianling marquisate; Nanyang followed, then conquest of Later Qin—Xingyang, Fufeng, Nan'an, Fengyi fell in turn.
units.literal: When Liu Yu campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi, he was appointed by emergency patent Grand Commandant aide and Administrator of Yiyang with noble rank Marquis of Qianling County; he was transferred Administrator of Nanyang and followed Liu Yu against Yao Hong, repeatedly attacking Xingyang, Fufeng, Nan'an, and Fengyi commanderies—everywhere victorious.

units.zh: 裕嘉之，以為龍驤將軍、秦州刺史。
units.en: Liu Yu rewarded him with Soaring Dragon general and Qinzhou inspector.
units.literal: Yu praised him and named him general Soaring Dragon and Inspector of Qinzhou.

units.zh: 裕留第二子義真為安西將軍、雍州刺史。
units.en: Liu Yu left Liu Yizhen as western pacifier and Yongzhou inspector.
units.literal: Yu left his second son Yizhen as general Who Pacifies the West and Inspector of Yongzhou.

units.zh: 以德祖為中兵參軍，領天水太守，從義真還。
units.en: Mao Dezu served as central corps aide and Tianshui magistrate on the withdrawal with Yizhen.
units.literal: He appointed Dezu central corps aide with concurrent Administrator of Tianshui, following Yizhen home.

units.zh: 裕以德祖督河東平陽二郡軍事、輔國將軍、河東太守，代劉遵考守蒲阪。
units.en: Liu Yu gave him Hedong-Pingyang command, supporting-state general, Hedong magistrate, Puban garrison—replacing Liu Zunkao.
units.literal: Yu made Dezu supervise Hedong and Pingyang military affairs, general Who Supports the State, Administrator of Hedong, replacing Liu Zunkao to hold Puban.

units.zh: 及河北覆敗，德祖全軍而歸。
units.en: Hebei's rout still saw Mao Dezu extract his corps whole.
units.literal: When the Hebei front collapsed, Dezu brought the entire army back intact.

units.zh: 裕方欲蕩平關洛，先以德祖督九郡軍事、冠軍將軍、滎陽京兆太守，以前後功，賜爵灌陽縣男，尋遷督司雍並三州諸軍事、冠軍將軍、司州刺史，戍武牢，為魏所沒。
units.en: Before the next Guan-Luo push Liu Yu named Mao Dezu champion over nine counties, Xingyang-Jingzhao magistrate, Guanyang baron, then Si-Yong-Bing governor with Sizhou inspectorate at Wulao—where Wei took him.
units.literal: Yu was about to level Guanzhong and Luoyang; first he made Dezu supervise nine commanderies' military affairs as Champion general and Administrator of Xingyang and Jingzhao; for successive merits he was granted Baron of Guanyang County; soon he was promoted supervisor of military affairs over Si, Yong, and Bing—three provinces—with Champion generalship and Inspectorship of Sizhou, garrisoning Wulao, where he was lost to Wei.

units.zh: 德祖次弟嶷，嶷弟辯，並有志節。
units.en: Younger brothers Mao Yi and Mao Bian shared fierce integrity.
units.literal: Dezu's next younger brother Yi and Yi's younger brother Bian both possessed determination and integrity.

units.zh: 嶷死于盧循之難，辯沒于魯宗之役，並奮不顧命，為世所歎。
units.en: Mao Yi fell in Lu Xun's rising; Mao Bian in Lu Zongzhi's war—both charged without thought for life.
units.literal: Yi died in Lu Xun's turmoil; Bian perished in Lu Zongzhi's campaign—both fought recklessly and were lamented by the age.

units.zh: 劉遐，字正長，廣平易陽人也。
units.en: Liu Xia, courtesy Zhengzhang, came from Yiyang in Guangping commandery.
units.literal: Liu Xia, styled Zhengzhang, was a man of Yiyang in Guangping.

units.zh: 性果毅，便弓馬，開豁勇壯。
units.en: He was bold and blunt, superb rider and archer, with fearless vigor.
units.literal: By nature he was resolute, handy with bow and horse, open-hearted, brave, and strong.

units.zh: 值天下大亂，遐為塢主，每擊賊，率壯士陷堅摧鋒，冀方比之張飛、關羽。
units.en: Amid collapse he ruled a river fort, charging vanguard like Zhang Fei or Guan Yu whenever raiders neared.
units.literal: When the realm fell into great chaos, Xia became fort master; whenever he struck bandits he led stalwarts to pierce armor and break spear-points; north of the Ji men compared him to Zhang Fei and Guan Yu.

units.zh: 鄉人冀州刺史邵續深器之，以女妻焉，遂壁於河濟之間，賊不敢逼。
units.en: Shao Xu of Jizhou admired him, married him into the family, and backed his stockade between the rivers until foes feared the ground.
units.literal: His townsman Inspector of Jizhou Shao Xu deeply esteemed him and gave him a daughter in marriage; he therefore walled between the Yellow and Ji rivers and bandits dared not press him.

units.zh: 遐間道遣使受元帝節度，朝廷嘉之，璽書慰勉，以為龍驤將軍、平原內史。
units.en: Secret couriers pledged him to Emperor Yuan; the throne answered with praise and named him Soaring Dragon general and Pingyuan secretary.
units.literal: Xia sent envoys by hidden paths to accept orders from Emperor Yuan; the court praised him with sealed edicts of comfort and encouragement and appointed him general Soaring Dragon and Interior Secretary of Pingyuan.

units.zh: 建武初，元帝令曰：「遐忠勇果毅，義誠可嘉。
units.en: At the beginning of the Jianwu era Emperor Yuan's order said, "Xia is loyal, brave, resolute, and righteous—conduct worthy of praise.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Jianwu era Emperor Yuan's order said: "Xia is loyal, brave, resolute, and righteous—conduct worthy of praise.

units.zh: 以遐為下邳內史，將軍如故。」
units.en: Make him Xiapi secretary while keeping his general's rank."
units.literal: Appoint Xia Interior Secretary of Xiapi with generalship unchanged."

units.zh: 初，沛人周堅，一名撫，與同郡周默因天下亂，各為塢主，以寇抄為事。
units.en: Pei natives Zhou Jian, alias Fu, and Zhou Mo crowned themselves fort chiefs and lived by plunder.
units.literal: At first Zhou Jian of Pei—also called Fu—and Zhou Mo of the same commandery, exploiting the realm's chaos, each became fort masters and lived by raiding.

units.zh: 默降祖逖，撫怒，遂襲殺默，以彭城叛，石勒遣騎援之。
units.en: Zhou Mo yielded to Zu Ti; Zhou Fu slew him, seized Pengcheng, and won Shi Le's riders.
units.literal: Mo surrendered to Zu Ti; Fu grew angry, attacked and killed Mo, rebelled at Pengcheng, and Shi Le sent cavalry to aid him.

units.zh: 詔遐領彭城內史，與徐州刺史蔡豹、太山太守徐龕共討撫，戰於寒山，撫敗走。
units.en: The court named Liu Xia Pengcheng secretary alongside Cai Bao and Xu Kan; Cold Mountain broke Zhou Fu.
units.literal: An edict ordered Xia to hold concurrent Interior Secretary of Pengcheng and together with Inspector of Xuzhou Cai Bao and Administrator of Taishan Xu Kan jointly punish Fu; they fought at Cold Mountain and Fu fled.

units.zh: 詔徙遐為臨淮太守。
units.en: Edict shifted him to Linhuai magistrate.
units.literal: An edict transferred Xia to Administrator of Linhuai.

units.zh: 徐龕復反，事平，以遐為北中郎將、兗州刺史。
units.en: After Xu Kan's second revolt cleared, Liu Xia took northern palace rank and Yanzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: When Xu Kan rebelled again and the affair was settled, Xia was appointed general of the Northern Palace Court and Inspector of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 太甯初，自彭城移屯泗口。
units.en: Early in the Taining era he shifted his camp from Pengcheng to Sikou.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Taining era he moved his camp from Pengcheng to Sikou.

units.zh: 王含反，遐與蘇峻俱赴京都。
units.en: When Wang Han rebelled, Liu Xia marched with Su Jun toward the capital.
units.literal: When Wang Han rebelled, Xia went with Su Jun to the capital.

units.zh: 含敗，隨丹陽尹溫嶠追含至於淮南，遐頗放兵虜掠。
units.en: After Han's defeat Liu Xia followed Danyang prefect Wen Qiao to Huainan and let his men loot freely.
units.literal: When Han was defeated, Xia followed Administrator of Danyang Wen Qiao in pursuing Han to Huainan, and Xia rather freely let his troops plunder captives.

units.zh: 嶠曰：「天道助順，故王含剿絕，不可因亂為亂也。」
units.en: Wen Qiao said, "Heaven aids the righteous, so Wang Han is destroyed; do not turn victory into fresh chaos."
units.literal: Qiao said, "Heaven aids the righteous, so Wang Han has been exterminated; one must not make disorder out of disorder."

units.zh: 遐深自陳而拜謝。
units.en: Liu Xia confessed his fault and apologized.
units.literal: Xia deeply confessed himself and bowed in apology.

units.zh: 事平，以功封泉陵公，遷散騎常侍、監淮北軍事、北中郎將、徐州刺史、假節，代王邃鎮淮陰。
units.en: After peace returned he was made duke of Quanling, ordinary attendant, Huai-north military supervisor, northern palace general, Xuzhou inspector with credential staff, and replaced Wang Sui at Huaiyin.
units.literal: When the affair was settled, for merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Quanling, promoted to Ordinary Attendant Cavalier, Supervisor of Military Affairs north of the Huai, General of the Northern Palace Court, Inspector of Xuzhou with credential staff, replacing Wang Sui to garrison Huaiyin.

units.zh: 咸和元年卒，追贈安北將軍。
units.en: He died in Xianhe 1 and was posthumously named general who pacifies the north.
units.literal: In the first year of Xianhe he died; posthumously he was granted General Who Pacifies the North.

units.zh: 子肇年幼，成帝以徐州授郗鑒，以郭默為北中郎將，領遐部曲。
units.en: Young Liu Zhao left Xuzhou to Xi Jian while Guo Mo absorbed Liu Xia's household troops.
units.literal: His son Zhao was young; Emperor Cheng assigned Xuzhou to Xi Jian and Guo Mo as general of the Northern Palace Court to lead Xia's personal corps.

units.zh: 遐妹夫田防及遐故將史迭、卞咸、李龍等不樂他屬，共立肇，襲遐故位以叛。
units.en: Brother-in-law Tian Fang and veterans Shi Die, Bian Xian, and Li Long refused new masters, crowned boy Zhao, and mutinied.
units.literal: Xia's brother-in-law Tian Fang and Xia's old commanders Shi Die, Bian Xian, Li Long and others disliked serving another master; together they raised Zhao, seized Xia's former post, and rebelled.

units.zh: 成帝遣郭默等率諸郡討之。
units.en: Guo Mo led county levies against them.
units.literal: Emperor Cheng dispatched Guo Mo and others leading various commanderies to punish them.

units.zh: 默等始上道，而臨淮太守劉矯率將士數百掩襲遐營，迭等迸走，斬田防及督護卞咸等，追斬迭、龍於下邳，傳首詣闕。
units.en: Before Guo Mo marched, Liu Jiao of Linhuai stormed the fort, scattered the plotters, beheaded Tian Fang and Bian Xian, ran down Shi Die and Li Long at Xiapi, and shipped heads south.
units.literal: Hardly had Mo and company set out when Administrator of Linhuai Liu Jiao led several hundred officers and men in a surprise raid on Xia's camp; Die and others scattered in flight; Jiao beheaded Tian Fang and protector Bian Xian and others; pursuing, he cut down Die and Long at Xiapi and sent heads to the capital.

units.zh: 遐母妻子參佐將士悉還建康。
units.en: Mother, wives, children, aides, and troops reached Jiankang alive.
units.literal: Xia's mother, wife, children, staff, and soldiers all returned to Jiankang.

units.zh: 遐妻驍果有父風。
units.en: Liu Xia's wife matched her father's ferocity.
units.literal: Xia's wife was fierce and resolute like her father.

units.zh: 遐嘗為石季龍所圍，妻單將數騎，拔遐出於萬眾之中。
units.en: When Shi Jilong ringed Liu Xia, she sliced through alone with a handful of horse and dragged him free.
units.literal: Once when Xia was surrounded by Shi Jilong, his wife alone led several riders and pulled Xia free from amid tens of thousands.

units.zh: 及田防等欲為亂，遐妻止之，不從，乃密起火燒甲杖都盡。
units.en: She forbade Tian Fang's coup; ignored, she torched the armory.
units.literal: When Tian Fang and others plotted revolt, Xia's wife stopped them; they would not listen, so she secretly set fires that burned armor and weapons to ash.

units.zh: 肇襲爵，官至散騎侍郎。
units.en: Liu Zhao inherited and climbed to palace gentleman attendant.
units.literal: Zhao inherited the nobility and rose to Gentleman Cavalier Attendant at the Palace.

units.zh: 肇卒，子舉嗣。
units.en: Liu Ju followed Liu Zhao.
units.literal: When Zhao died, his son Ju inherited.

units.zh: 卒，子遵之嗣。
units.en: Next came Liu Dunzhi.
units.literal: When he died, his son Dunzhi inherited.

units.zh: 卒，子伯齡嗣。
units.en: Liu Boling succeeded.
units.literal: When he died, his son Boling inherited.

units.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
units.en: Liu Song erased the fief.
units.literal: When Song received the abdication, the principality was abolished.

units.zh: 鄧岳，字伯山，陳郡人也。
units.en: Deng Yue, courtesy Boshan, came from Chen commandery.
units.literal: Deng Yue, styled Boshan, was a man of Chen Commandery.

units.zh: 本名岳，以犯康帝諱，改為嶽，後竟改名為岱焉。
units.en: Born Deng Yue, he swapped graphs for Kang's taboo to Deng Yue variant, then settled on Deng Dai.
units.literal: His original given name was Yue; because it violated Emperor Kang's taboo he changed it to Yue with the mountain radical, and later finally renamed himself Dai.

units.zh: 少有將帥才略，為王敦參軍。
units.en: Young Deng Yue showed command gifts on Wang Dun's staff.
units.literal: In youth he possessed strategic talent and became Wang Dun's aide.

units.zh: 轉從事中郎、西陽太守。
units.en: Promotion brought attendant clerk and Xiyang magistrate.
units.literal: He was transferred attendant clerk and Administrator of Xiyang.

units.zh: 王含構產逆，嶽領兵隨含向京都。
units.en: Wang Han's coup drew Deng Yue's column toward Jiankang.
units.literal: When Wang Han plotted treason, Yue led troops following Han toward the capital.

units.zh: 及含敗，岳與周撫俱奔蠻王向蠶。
units.en: Defeat sent Deng Yue and Zhou Fu to Barbarian King Xiang Can.
units.literal: When Han was defeated, Yue fled together with Zhou Fu to the Yi chieftain Xiang Can.

units.zh: 後遇赦，與撫俱出。
units.en: Amnesty freed him with Zhou Fu.
units.literal: Later encountering an amnesty, he emerged together with Fu.

units.zh: 久之，司徒王導命為從事中郎，後復為西陽太守。
units.en: Wang Dao later restored him to attendant clerk and Xiyang.
units.literal: After a long while Minister of Education Wang Dao ordered him attendant clerk; later he again became Administrator of Xiyang.

units.zh: 及蘇峻反，平南將軍溫嶠遣嶽與督護王愆期、鄱陽太守紀睦等率舟軍赴難。
units.en: Su Jun's rising saw Wen Qiao send Deng Yue, Wang Yanqi, and Ji Mu downstream.
units.literal: When Su Jun rebelled, general Who Pacifies the South Wen Qiao dispatched Yue together with protector Wang Yanqi, Administrator of Poyang Ji Mu, and others leading river forces to the rescue.

units.zh: 峻平，還郡。
units.en: Peace took him home to Xiyang.
units.literal: After Jun was crushed he returned to his commandery.

units.zh: 郭默之殺劉胤也，大司馬陶侃使岳率西陽之眾討之。
units.en: Guo Mo's killing of Liu Yin brought Tao Kan's order for Deng Yue to march from Xiyang.
units.literal: When Guo Mo murdered Liu Yin, Grand Marshal Tao Kan ordered Yue to lead Xiyang's host against him.

units.zh: 默平，遷督交廣二州軍事、建武將軍、領平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節，錄前後勳，封宜城縣伯。
units.en: Victory stacked titles: Jiao-Guang overseer, mighty-display general, Yue colonel, Guangzhou inspector, credential staff, baron of Yicheng.
units.literal: After Mo was crushed he was promoted to supervise military affairs of Jiao and Guang—two provinces—general Who Displays Martial Might, concurrent Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou with credential staff; recording successive merits he was enfeoffed Baron of Yicheng County.

units.zh: 咸康三年，嶽遣軍伐夜郎，破之，加督寧州，進征虜將軍，遷平南將軍。
units.en: Xiankang third year brought conquest of Yelang, added Ningzhou watch, caitiff general, southern pacifier.
units.literal: In the third year of Xiankang Yue dispatched troops to attack Yelang, crushed them, added supervision of Ningzhou, advanced to general Who Conquers the Caitiffs, and was promoted general Who Pacifies the South.

units.zh: 卒，子遐嗣。
units.en: Son Deng Xia succeeded.
units.literal: When he died, his son Xia inherited.

units.zh: 遐字應遠。
units.en: Deng Xia took courtesy Yingyuan.
units.literal: Xia styled Yingyuan.

units.zh: 勇力絕人，氣蓋當時，時人方之樊噲。
units.en: Strength and swagger rivaled Fan Kuai in gossip.
units.literal: His courage and strength surpassed others and his spirit overshadowed the age; men of the time compared him to Fan Kuai.

units.zh: 桓溫以為參軍，數從溫征伐，曆冠軍將軍，數郡太守，號為名將。
units.en: Huan Wen's wars forged champion posts and county seats until Deng Xia ranked among storied captains.
units.literal: Huan Wen employed him as aide; he repeatedly followed Wen on campaigns, rose through Champion general and several magistracies, and was famed as a noted general.

units.zh: 襄陽城北沔水中有蛟，常為人害，遐遂拔劍入水，蛟繞其足，遐揮劍截蛟數段而出。
units.en: A river monster plagued Xiangyang; Deng Xia waded in, let it twist his legs, and carved it to pieces.
units.literal: North of Xiangyang in the Han River lay a river-dragon that habitually harmed people; Xia drew his sword, entered the water, the dragon coiled his legs, and Xia slashed it into several segments and emerged.

units.zh: 枋頭之役，溫既懷恥忿，且忌憚遐之勇果，因免遐官，尋卒。
units.en: Fangtou's humiliation made Huan Wen jealous of Deng Xia's nerve—he stripped him and Xia died soon after.
units.literal: At the Fangtou campaign Wen nursed shame and rage and also feared Xia's courage and resolution; therefore he dismissed Xia from office; soon Xia died.

units.zh: 甯康中，追贈廬陵太守。
units.en: Ningkang years posthumously named him Luling magistrate.
units.literal: During Ningkang he was posthumously honored Administrator of Luling.

units.zh: 岳弟逸，字茂山，亦有武幹。
units.en: Brother Deng Yi shared martial gifts.
units.literal: Yue's younger brother Yi, styled Maoshan, also possessed martial capacity.

units.zh: 嶽卒後，以逸監交廣州、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史、假節。
units.en: Deng Yue's death handed Deng Yi Jiao-Guang command, mighty-display rank, Yue colonel, Guangzhou inspector, credential staff.
units.literal: After Yue died, Yi was appointed supervisor of Jiao and Guangzhou, general Who Displays Martial Might, Colonel Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou with credential staff.

units.zh: 朱序，字次倫，義陽人也。
units.en: Zhu Xu, courtesy Cilun, hailed from Yiyang.
units.literal: Zhu Xu, styled Cilun, was a man of Yiyang.

units.zh: 父燾，以才幹曆西蠻校尉、益州刺史。
units.en: Father Zhu Tao climbed to western Yi colonel and Yizhou inspector.
units.literal: His father Tao rose through talent to Colonel Who Subdues the Western Yi and Inspector of Yizhou.

units.zh: 序世為名將，累遷鷹揚將軍、江夏相。
units.en: Generals ran in the blood; Zhu Xu rose to spreading-might general and Jiangxia chancellor.
units.literal: For generations the house produced noted generals; Xu was repeatedly promoted general Who Spreads Might and Chancellor of Jiangxia.

units.zh: 興甯末，梁州刺史司馬勳反，桓溫表序為征討都護往討之，以功拜征虜將軍，封襄平子。
units.en: Sima Xun's Liangzhou revolt sent Zhu Xu under Huan Wen's banner—merit won caitiff general and Xiangping viscount.
units.literal: Near the end of the Xingning era Inspector of Liangzhou Sima Xun rebelled; Huan Wen memorialized Xu as supreme protector for the punitive expedition; for merit he was appointed general Who Conquers the Caitiffs and enfeoffed Viscount of Xiangping.

units.zh: 太和中，遷兗州刺史。
units.en: Taihe brought Yanzhou inspectorate.
units.literal: During the Taihe era he was transferred Inspector of Yanzhou.

units.zh: 時長城人錢弘聚党百餘人，藏匿原鄉山。
units.en: Qian Hong holed up on Yuanxiang Mountain with a hundred blades.
units.literal: At that time Qian Hong of Changcheng gathered a band of over a hundred men and hid on Yuanxiang Mountain.

units.zh: 以序為中軍司馬、吳興太守。
units.en: Court named Zhu Xu central army marshal and Wuxing magistrate.
units.literal: Xu was appointed marshal of the Central Army and Administrator of Wuxing.

units.zh: 序至郡，討擒之。
units.en: He swept the hills and caged Qian Hong.
units.literal: When Xu reached the commandery he attacked and captured him.

units.zh: 事訖，還兗州。
units.en: Duty done, he reclaimed Yanzhou.
units.literal: When the affair concluded he returned to Yanzhou.

units.zh: 甯康初，拜使持節、監沔中諸軍事、南中郎將、梁州刺史，鎮襄陽。
units.en: Ningkang opened with credential staff, Han River command, southern palace general, Liangzhou inspector at Xiangyang.
units.literal: At the beginning of Ningkang he was appointed credential bearer, supervisor of all military affairs on the Han River, General of the Southern Palace Court, Inspector of Liangzhou, garrisoning Xiangyang.

units.zh: 是歲，苻堅遣其將苻不等率眾圍序，序固守，賊糧將盡，率眾苦攻之。
units.en: Fu Jian's Fu Bu besieged Xiangyang until supplies failed, then hurled desperate assaults.
units.literal: That year Fu Jian dispatched general Fu Bu and others leading a host to besiege Xu; Xu held firm; enemy grain nearly exhausted and they pressed the assault with full strength.

units.zh: 初，苻丕之來攻也，序母韓自登城履行，謖西北角當先受弊，遂領百餘婢並城中女子於其角斜築城二十餘丈。
units.en: Lady Han walked the walls, saw the northwest would buckle first, and piled twenty-plus zhang of earth there with maids and townswomen.
units.literal: At first, when Fu Bu came to attack, Xu's mother Lady Han herself climbed the wall to inspect and judged the northwest corner would suffer harm first; she therefore led more than a hundred maids together with women of the city to build slanting ramparts twenty-plus zhang at that corner.

units.zh: 賊攻西北角，果潰，眾便固新築城。
units.en: The foe smashed the old northwest shoulder; defenders slid onto Lady Han's fresh berm.
units.literal: The bandits assaulted the northwest corner and it indeed collapsed; the host then held firm on the newly built wall.

units.zh: 丕遂引退。
units.en: Fu Bu quit the siege.
units.literal: Bu therefore withdrew.

units.zh: 襄陽人謂此城為夫人城。
units.en: Locals still call it the Lady's Wall.
units.literal: People of Xiangyang call this rampart Lady's Wall.

units.zh: 序累戰破賊，人情勞懈，又以賊退稍遠，疑未能來，守備不謹，督護李伯護密與賊相應，襄陽遂沒，序陷於苻堅。
units.en: Victory bred slack; Zhu Xu assumed distance meant peace; Li Bohu betrayed the gates to Fu Jian.
units.literal: Xu repeatedly fought and defeated bandits; morale grew weary and lax; moreover because the bandits had withdrawn somewhat far he doubted they would come again and guarding grew careless; protector Li Bohu secretly communicated with bandits; Xiangyang therefore fell and Xu was trapped by Fu Jian.

units.zh: 堅殺伯護徇之，以其不忠也。
units.en: Fu Jian executed Li Bohu as the traitor he was.
units.literal: Jian executed Bohu as a warning because he was disloyal.

units.zh: 序欲逃歸，潛至宜陽，藏夏揆家。
units.en: Zhu Xu slipped toward Jin lines and hid with Xia Kui.
units.literal: Xu wished to flee home and secretly reached Yiyang, hiding with Xia Kui's household.

units.zh: 堅疑揆，收之，序乃詣苻暉自首，堅嘉而不問，以為尚書。
units.en: Suspicion fell on Xia Kui; Zhu Xu surrendered to Fu Hui instead and Fu Jian admired him into minister rank.
units.literal: Jian suspected Kui and seized him; Xu therefore presented himself to Fu Hui to confess; Jian praised him and did not punish him, appointing him minister of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 太元中，苻堅南侵，謝石率眾距之。
units.en: Taiyuan brought Fu Jian south against Xie Shi.
units.literal: During the Taiyuan era Fu Jian invaded south and Xie Shi led troops to resist him.

units.zh: 時堅大兵尚在項，苻融以三十萬眾先至。
units.en: Fu Jian's core host lingered at Xiang while Fu Rong landed three hundred thousand.
units.literal: At that time Jian's main army was still at Xiang; Fu Rong arrived first with three hundred thousand.

units.zh: 堅遣序說謝石，稱己兵威。
units.en: Fu Jian sent Zhu Xu to awe Xie Shi with numbers.
units.literal: Jian dispatched Xu to persuade Xie Shi, boasting his army's might.

units.zh: 序反謂石曰：「若堅百萬之眾悉到，莫可與敵，及其未會，擊之，可以得志。」
units.en: Zhu Xu whispered: wait for the million and you lose—hit Fu Jian now while columns straggle."
units.literal: Xu instead told Shi: "If Jian's million troops all arrive none can oppose them; strike before they assemble and you may succeed."

units.zh: 於是石遣謝琰選勇士八千人涉肥水挑戰。
units.en: Xie Shi ordered Xie Yan across the Fei with eight thousand picked men.
units.literal: Thereupon Shi dispatched Xie Yan to pick eight thousand warriors to ford the Fei River and offer challenge.

units.zh: 堅眾小卻，序時在其軍後，唱云：「堅敗！」
units.en: Fu Jian's lines eased backward; Zhu Xu howled from the rear that Fu Jian had fallen."
units.literal: Jian's host stepped slightly back; Xu was then behind their lines and shouted: "Jian is defeated!"

units.zh: 眾遂大奔，序乃得歸。
units.en: Panic routed Fu Jian and Zhu Xu sprinted home.
units.literal: The host thereupon fled in panic and Xu was able to return.

units.zh: 拜龍驤將軍、琅邪內史，轉揚州豫州五郡軍事、豫州刺史，屯洛陽。
units.en: Rewards piled: Soaring Dragon, Langye secretary, five-county Yang-Yu command, Yuzhou inspector at Luoyang.
units.literal: He was appointed general Soaring Dragon, Interior Secretary of Langye, transferred supervisor of military affairs over five Yangzhou and Yuzhou commanderies with Inspectorship of Yuzhou, garrisoning Luoyang.

units.zh: 後丁零翟遼反，序遣將軍秦膺、童斌與淮泗諸郡共討之。
units.en: Zhai Liao's Dingling revolt drew Qin Ying and Tong Bin from Zhu Xu.
units.literal: Later Dingling chief Zhai Liao rebelled; Xu dispatched generals Qin Ying and Tong Bin together with Huai and Si commanderies to punish him.

units.zh: 又監兗青二州諸軍事、二州刺史，將軍如故，進鎮彭城。
units.en: He added Yan-Qing oversight, twin inspectors, old rank, Pengcheng seat.
units.literal: He additionally supervised military affairs of Yan and Qing—two provinces—with concurrent dual inspectorship, general as before, advancing headquarters to Pengcheng.

units.zh: 序求鎮淮陰，帝許焉。
units.en: He traded up for Huaiyin and the throne agreed.
units.literal: Xu requested to garrison Huaiyin; the emperor granted it.

units.zh: 翟遼又使其子釗寇陳潁，序還遣秦膺討釗，走之，拜征虜將軍。
units.en: Zhai Liao's son Zhai Zhao raided Chen-Ying; Qin Ying threw him back and Zhu Xu gained caitiff general.
units.literal: Zhai Liao again sent his son Zhai Zhao to raid Chen and Ying; Xu returned and dispatched Qin Ying against Zhao, drove him off, and was appointed general Who Conquers the Caitiffs.

units.zh: 表求運江州米十萬斛，布五千匹以資軍費，詔聽之。
units.en: He begged one hundred thousand hu from Jiangzhou plus five thousand bolts—approved.
units.literal: He memorialized requesting one hundred thousand hu of grain from Jiangzhou and five thousand bolts of cloth to supply military expenses; an edict approved.

units.zh: 加都督司、雍、梁、秦四州軍事。
units.en: Four-province Si-Yong-Liang-Qin command followed.
units.literal: He was additionally named supervisor of military affairs over Si, Yong, Liang, and Qin—four provinces.

units.zh: 帝遣廣威將軍、河南太守楊佺期，南陽太守趙睦，各領兵千人隸序。
units.en: Yang Quanqi of Henan and Zhao Mu of Nanyang brought a thousand men each to Zhu Xu.
units.literal: The emperor dispatched general Who Displays Martial Glory and Administrator of Henan Yang Quanqi and Administrator of Nanyang Zhao Mu, each leading a thousand men under Xu's command.

units.zh: 序又表求故荊州刺史桓石生府田百頃，並谷八萬斛，給之。
units.en: He claimed Huan Shisheng's hundred qing and eighty thousand hu—granted.
units.literal: Xu further memorialized requesting the hundred qing of farmland and eighty thousand hu of grain formerly attached to former Inspector of Jingzhou Huan Shisheng's office; they were granted.

units.zh: 仍戍洛陽，衛山陵也。
units.en: He stayed at Luoyang guarding Jin mausolea.
units.literal: He still garrisoned Luoyang to guard the imperial tombs.

units.zh: 其後慕容永率眾向洛陽，序自河陰北濟，與永偽將王次等相遇，乃戰于沁水，次改走，斬其支將勿支首。
units.en: Murong Yong drew Zhu Xu north from Heyin; Qin River broke Wang Ci and took Wuzhi's head.
units.literal: Later Murong Yong led troops toward Luoyang; Xu crossed north from Heyin, encountered Yong's deputy Wang Ci and others, fought at the Qin River—Ci fled—and beheaded deputy Wuzhi.

units.zh: 參軍趙睦、江夏相桓不才追永，破之於太行。
units.en: Zhao Mu and Huan Bucai chased Murong Yong into Taihang and broke him.
units.literal: Aides Zhao Mu and Chancellor of Jiangxia Huan Bucai pursued Yong and defeated him at Taihang.

units.zh: 永歸上黨。
units.en: Murong Yong fled to Shangdang.
units.literal: Yong returned to Shangdang.

units.zh: 時楊楷聚眾數千，在湖陝，聞永敗，遣任子詣序乞降。
units.en: Yang Kai at Huxia offered surrender after Yong's rout.
units.literal: At that time Yang Kai gathered several thousand men at Huxia; hearing Yong's defeat he sent heir Ren to Xu seeking surrender.

units.zh: 序追永至上黨之白水，與永相持二旬。
units.en: Zhu Xu dogged Murong Yong to Baishui for twenty days.
units.literal: Xu pursued Yong to Baishui in Shangdang and faced him for twenty days.

units.zh: 聞翟遼欲向金墉，乃還，遂攻翟釗于石門，遣參軍趙蕃破翟遼於懷縣，遼宵遁。
units.en: News of Zhai Liao aiming at Golden Rampart spun Zhu Xu back—Stone Gate struck Zhai Zhao, Zhao Fan whipped Zhai Liao at Huai, who vanished overnight.
units.literal: Hearing Zhai Liao meant to strike the Golden Rampart fortress he returned, attacked Zhai Zhao at Stone Gate, dispatched aide Zhao Fan to defeat Zhai Liao at Huai County; Liao fled by night.

units.zh: 序退次洛陽，留鷹揚將軍朱党戍石門。
units.en: He regrouped at Luoyang leaving Zhu Dang at Stone Gate.
units.literal: Xu withdrew to halt at Luoyang and left general Who Spreads Might Zhu Dang to hold Stone Gate.

units.zh: 序仍使子略督護洛城，趙蕃為助。
units.en: Son Zhu Lue guarded Luoyang with Zhao Fan.
units.literal: Xu still ordered son Lue to supervise defense of Luoyang city with Zhao Fan assisting.

units.zh: 序還襄陽。
units.en: Zhu Xu rode home to Xiangyang.
units.literal: Xu returned to Xiangyang.

units.zh: 會稽王道子以序勝負相補，不加褒貶。
units.en: Prince Daozi judged Zhu Xu's wins and losses a wash—no medal, no lash.
units.literal: Prince of Kuaiji Wang Daozi deemed Xu's victories and defeats balanced each other and added neither praise nor blame.

units.zh: 其後東羌校尉竇沖欲入漢川，安定人皇甫釗、京兆人周勳等謀納之。
units.en: Dou Chong aimed at Hanzhong; Huangfu Zhao and Zhou Xun meant to open the gate.
units.literal: Later Colonel of the Eastern Qiang Dou Chong wished to enter Hanzhong; Huangfu Zhao of Anding and Zhou Xun of Jingzhao plotted to admit him.

units.zh: 梁州刺史周瓊失巴西三郡，眾寡力弱，告急於序，序遣將軍皇甫貞率眾赴之。
units.en: Zhou Qiong's triple loss brought Zhu Xu's column under Huangfu Zhen.
units.literal: Inspector of Liangzhou Zhou Qiong lost three Ba-Xi commanderies; his host was few and weak; he urgently appealed to Xu; Xu dispatched general Huangfu Zhen with troops to hurry there.

units.zh: 沖據長安東，釗、勳散走。
units.en: Dou Chong seized Chang'an's east flank while plotters ran.
units.literal: Chong occupied east of Chang'an; Zhao and Xun scattered in flight.

units.zh: 序以老病，累表解職，不許。
units.en: Age and sickness drove resignation pleas—denied.
units.literal: Xu, citing age and illness, repeatedly memorialized to resign; permission was refused.

units.zh: 詔斷表，遂輒去任。
units.en: Edicts barred more excuses; he quit anyway.
units.literal: An edict cut off memorials; he nevertheless departed post.

units.zh: 數旬，歸罪廷尉，詔原不問。
units.en: He presented himself to the minister of justice and won blanket pardon.
units.literal: After several tens of days he surrendered himself to the minister of justice; an edict pardoned him without inquiry.

units.zh: 太元十八年卒，贈左將軍、散騎常侍。
units.en: Taiyuan eighteen ended his life; posthumous left general and ordinary attendant followed.
units.literal: He died in the eighteenth year of Taiyuan; posthumously honored general of the Left with ordinary attendant cavalier.

units.zh: 史臣曰：晉氏淪喪，播遷江表，內難薦臻，外虞不息，經略之道，是所未弘，將帥之功，無聞焉爾。
units.en: Historians add: refugee Jin faced coup within and raid without—little grand strategy, thinner laurels for captains.
units.literal: The historians remark: When Jin lost the Central Plains and shifted south of the Yangzi, inner calamities piled up without cease and outer peril never rested—the arts of grand strategy were never broadly developed, and true merit among generals is scarcely heard.

units.zh: 遜、豹、宣、胤服勤於太興之間，毛、鄧、劉、朱馳騖乎咸和之後。
units.en: Wang Xun, Cai Bao, Huan Xuan, and Liu Yin wore themselves out in Emperor Yuan's Taixing reign; Mao Bao, Deng Yue, Liu Xia, and Zhu Si chased glory once Xianhe arrived.
units.literal: Xun, Bao, Xuan, and Yin bore heavy service between the Taixing years; Mao, Deng, Liu, and Zhu raced their chargers after the Xianhe era.

units.zh: 雖人不逮古，亦足列於當世焉。
units.en: They fell short of legendary exemplars yet deserved places among their contemporaries.
units.literal: Although none matched men of high antiquity, they still suffice to stand among peers of their own age.

units.zh: 贊曰：氣分淮海，災流瀍澗。
units.en: Verdict runs: fortune fractured between Huai and the eastern sea; calamity flooded the Chan and Jian valleys.
units.literal: The encomium says: Vital breath split Huai and sea; disaster spilled Chan and Jian.

units.zh: 覆類玄蚖，興微《鴻雁》。
units.en: Collapse coiled like shadow reptiles; even faint renewal echoed 《Wild Geese》 on weary wings.
units.literal: Ruin wrapped folk like black creeping things; amid faint revival sounded 《Wild Geese》.

units.zh: 鼓鞞在聽，《兔罝》有作。
units.en: Battle drums hammered the courts; recruiting songs such as 《The Rabbit Snare》 rang out again.
units.literal: War-drums filled every ear; 《The Rabbit Snare》 found makers once more.

units.zh: 赳赳群英，勤茲王略。
units.en: Staunch captains shouldered the throne's wider strategy with relentless grit.
units.literal: Bold, bold that band of champions—they strained every nerve for the royal plan.
